title: Why the Projection for the Houston Rockets to Earn the 3rd Seed in the West is Realistic
description: The projection of Houston finishing with a 51-31 record is achievable for a few reasons.
fullText:
On August 24, 2026, ESPN revealed its projected standings for the upcoming 2026-27. ESPN projected the Houston Rockets to finish as the third seed, tied with the Denver Nuggets. Both teams would finish with a 51-31 record.

Considering that the Rockets finished the last two seasons with a 52-30 record, these projections are reasonable. Along with Houston's recent roster additions, the development of the young core, and the return of injured players, the third seed seems achievable if not likely.

Houston signed Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanović from free agency this summer, adding much-needed roster depth and veteran leadership. Smart's strong and motivating locker-room presence, ball-handling and playmaking skills, and elite perimeter defense will improve the second unit. Bogdanović's signing adds a three-point threat to the team, which the Rockets lacked last season.Houston has a very strong young core.

Amen Thompson has developed into one of the best young two-way players in the NBA. Thompson's length and speed make him one of the most versatile perimeter defenders. He also has a strong interior presence. Out of his average of 18.3 points per game, 12.1 of those points came directly in the paint. His athleticism and creativity make him an elite finisher in the paint, which is proven by his 70.5% field goal percentage in the restricted area.

Amen Thompson's weakness is his three-point and mid-range shooting, in which he averaged an abysmal 21.6% and 27.8%, respectively. However, Houston hired Chip Engelland to improve the team's shooting. Engelland's track record shows that he can work his magic and make Thompson a respectable shooter.

Engelland will also focus on improving the 24-year-old Alperen Şengün. Şengün shot a poor 30.5% from deep and 35.5% from mid-range. On top of this, he also averages 69.1% from the free-throw line.

If Engelland can improve their shooting, it will force the opposing teams to spread out to the perimeter, thereby creating space in the paint and widening the cutting lanes.

Houston's roster will also be bolstered by the addition of both Steven Adams and Fred VanVleet. VanVleet missed the entire 2025-26 season due to an ACL tear, but is now healthy and increasingly motivated for the upcoming season. Adams suffered a severe ankle sprain in January, missing the rest of the season.

These improvements to the Rockets' roster should be enough to land them in the top five of the Western Conference. Pinnacle has the over/under for Houston's total season wins at 47.5, meaning that the team will have to perform only slightly above the sharp predictions to earn the third seed and win 51 games.

The indication is that although the prediction is not probable, it is certainly realistic. Will the improvements in the roster and management be enough?

title: Entering contract year, Cason Wallace shows off scoring bag in offseason run
description: Entering contract year, Cason Wallace shows off scoring bag in offseason run.
fullText:
In the final week of August, we're in the dog days of summer. Very little is going on in the NBA world. Most of the offseason homework is done and teams are awaiting training camps to start. Right now, everybody is bored out of their mind. But right around the corner, we're about to see the yearly marathon restart.

The Oklahoma City Thunder enter the 2026-27 season as a co-title favorite — alongside the San Antonio Spurs. Even with their cost-cutting moves this offseason, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren should be enough to keep you in the title hunt.

But with Lu Dort and others out the door, Cason Wallace could be in line for a massive promotion. The 22-year-old will likely become a full-time starter this upcoming season. He'll no longer have to call himself the unofficial sixth starter as he has over the first three seasons of his rich basketball career. He'll also get more opportunities to grow on offense.

With a vacuum of possessions and shot attempts up for grabs, Wallace should see an uptick in offensive production. No longer will he have to settle for catch-and-shoot looks with the occasional downhill drive. Now, OKC's success could depend on his development on that side of the floor. It looks like he's taking it seriously this summer.

Wallace showed off his ball-handling creativity in a recent open gym run. He also showed he can pull up from deep outside. In a social media video that highlighted his best plays, he showed some finesse around his driving game as he kissed the ball off the glass for a layup. Everything is set up for him to be a double-digit scorer for the first time in his career this upcoming season. It's now about running away with that opportunity.

These summer months are when NBA players usually make the most strides in their respective games. The downtime allows them to work on their craft undisturbed. It'll be interesting to see how Wallace looks as he's about to enter his fourth NBA season already.

Splitting doubles, snaking the PnR, spin moves into the screener, relocating to open space, and sooooo much more comfortable off the dribble and into his shot, stepback, pull-ups, he’s gonna be a monster 😈 pic.twitter.com/Wx6mdLvm60

title: Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad: How to Watch Today as Madrid’s Injury Problems Grow
description: Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad takes place at the Santiago Bernabéu on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, in the rearranged La Liga Matchday 1 fixture. Kick-off is set for 9:00 p.m. CEST, or 8:00 p.m.
fullText:
Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad takes place at the Santiago Bernabéu on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, in the rearranged La Liga Matchday 1 fixture. Kick-off is set for 9:00 p.m. CEST, or 8:00 p.m. BST. Real Madrid will play their first home league game of the season after opening the campaign with a 2-1 win away to Espanyol.

Real Sociedad, meanwhile, arrive in Madrid after losing 1-0 to Real Betis. The fixture was moved from its original date because several Real Madrid players were still involved in the 2026 World Cup.

José Mourinho will lead Real Madrid into his first competitive home match since returning to the club. Pellegrino Matarazzo will take charge of Real Sociedad as both teams look to improve their early league position.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad will see Mourinho manage a squad affected by early injuries. Éder Militão and Rodrygo are unavailable, while Ferland Mendy, Raúl Asencio and Thiago Pitarch are also sidelined according to the match information supplied. Real Madrid started the season with a 2-1 win at Espanyol, with new signing Carlos Espí scoring the 90th-minute winner. Jude Bellingham had earlier put Madrid ahead before Espanyol equalized.

Real Sociedad began with a 1-0 defeat against Real Betis. Mikel Oyarzabal is among the key players available to Matarazzo, while Álvaro Odriozola remains out with a long-term knee injury. Gonçalo Guedes and Pablo Marín faced fitness checks before the match.

The confirmed Real Madrid lineup includes Thibaut Courtois, Denzel Dumfries, Álvaro Carreras, Federico Valverde, Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen, Arda Güler, Bernardo Silva, Kylian Mbappé, Jude Bellingham and Vinícius Júnior. Mourinho has selected a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Real Sociedad's starting team includes Álex Remiro, Jon Aramburu, Sergio Gómez, Carlos Soler, Igor Zubeldia, Jon Martín, Takefusa Kubo, Yangel Herrera, Orri Steinn Óskarsson and Luka Sučić, with the final attacking position listed for Gonçalo Guedes in the confirmed lineup. Matarazzo also uses a 4-2-3-1 shape. Oyarzabal is among the substitutes.

Real Madrid have won four of their last five meetings with Real Sociedad. Their most recent meeting at the Bernabéu ended in a 4-1 Real Madrid victory in February 2026, with Vinícius Júnior scoring twice. The teams also played out a 4-4 Copa del Rey draw in April 2025.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad kicks off at 9:00 p.m. CEST at the Santiago Bernabéu. Real Madrid's official schedule confirms the match was postponed from Matchday 1 because of World Cup commitments.

In Spain, the match is listed on Orange TV and Movistar LaLiga. Viewers outside Spain can also follow the match through regional broadcasters. Fans in the UK can use Premier Sports or LaLigaTV, while DAZN has coverage in Italy and Germany.

In the US, ESPN+ and ESPN Deportes will carry La Liga, with TSN+ serving viewers in Canada. beIN Sports covers the Middle East and North Africa, while SuperSport provides La Liga coverage across Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Jeshaun Jones Suspended for First Three Games of Regular Season
description: Not great timing for a fringe player
fullText:
A member of the Minnesota Vikings who is currently fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster has just seen his chances of not being a part of the team's final cuts increase dramatically. . .for the wrong reasons.

The National Football League has informed Vikings' wide receiver Jeshaun Jones that he will be suspended for the first three games of the 2026 regular season for violating the league's substance abuse policy. He can continue participating in the team's preseason program, including Friday's game in Denver against the Broncos, before starting his suspension on 30 August.

Jones was reportedly arrested outside of Tampa on 18 April for refusing to submit to a blood test to determine his blood-alcohol level. He pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of reckless driving last month, with a sentence that includes twelve months of probation.

While Jones' chances of making the active roster appear to be slim, he would not count against the 53-man roster during the time he is on the suspended list if the Vikings wanted to keep him around. Jones, who leads the Vikings in receiving yardage through the first two preseason games, has been on the team's practice squad the past two seasons and would likely be a candidate to be there again this season.

Jones will be eligible to return at the start of Week 4, so we will see if this incident plays any role in whether or not the team brings him back or decides to cut ties with him completely.

title: 49ers Owner Jed York Used Fake Name When Contacting Prostitution Ad Before Trailer Park Arrest
description: York was arrested Sunday at an Ohio trailer park after apparently attempting to meet with who he believed was a prostitute.
fullText:
49ers owner Jed York contacted a fake prostitution service under a false name multiple times before his Sunday morning arrest at an Ohio trailer park, according to multiple reports that cited an incident record, shedding more light on the circumstances that briefly put York in jail.

York used a pseudonym when he contacted a fictitious prostitution advertisement three times, ESPN reported, citing an incident report that said York identified himself as "Joe."

The ad was created by an undercover officer and resulted in the officer offering to meet York at a trailer park in East Palestine, Ohio.

The 49ers owner inquired about sexual services and was told full service sexual activity would cost $160, with unprotected sex costing $20 more, according to the incident report, which was also reported by the San Francisco Chronicle.

York was arrested in a sting operation at the trailer park, which he drove to in a rental car while carrying $160 in cash, according to the reports.

York pleaded no contest to charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, being ordered to pay $1,150 in fines in addition to a two-day jail sentence, though one day was credited for time already served.

Forbes has reached out to the 49ers for comment.

We estimate York's mother Denise and her family's net worth at $8.5 billion. The family owns a majority of the 49ers, which ranked No. 5 on Forbes' 2025 list of the NFL's most valuable teams.

"From a football standpoint, it has no effect on us," 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters Tuesday. "I mean, as far as what we do day to day, what we talk about and [it] hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today, it doesn't have to do with what happens on the field."

An NFL spokesperson told ESPN the incident would be reviewed under its personal conduct policy.

York's arrest comes months after he filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle Belluomini. York and Belluomini, who are separated, married in 2011 and have two children together. York became the 49ers CEO in 2008 and was the team's principal owner by 2024, after purchasing enough shares from his mother. The 49ers, which have lost all three of their Super Bowl appearances since York became CEO, have experienced a rocky pre-season off the field. Shanahan was involved in a head-on vehicle collision in July, suffering lacerations, fractures and a concussion. He publicly took responsibility for the incident and is recovering as he continues tending to coaching duties. The driver of the other vehicle, a 21-year-old woman, was not seriously injured.

description: The 2026-27 San Antonio Spurs season is one that is facing sky-high expectations.The Spurs are coming off of a defeat in the 2026 NBA Finals. fullText:
The 2026-27 San Antonio Spurs season is one that is facing sky-high expectations.

The Spurs are coming off of a defeat in the 2026 NBA Finals. The sobering loss isn't lessening hopes of bringing the first title to San Antonio since 2014, however.

The championship aspirations are extending beyond this season as well. The blend of present expectations and future anticipation should undeniably excite Spurs fans.

GettyDylan Harper is posturing to have a year two breakout.

The Spurs' future is extremely bright according to the consensus. Stephen Noh of Sporting News is further asserting this sentiment, as he projects the Spurs as the number one team in the NBA three years down the line.

San Antonio ranks directly ahead of Western Conference rivals in the Oklahoma City Thunder and Los Angeles Lakers here. This is an incredible vote of confidence in a franchise that still faces challenges despite being lush with assets.

Victor Wembanyama taking a discount in his rookie-scale contract makes it much more simple to build a sufficient roster around him. Dylan Harper is already establishing himself as one of the brightest two-way stars at the guard position in the league (Crafted NBA). Breakout star Stephon Castle is ready to take another step in year three in his own right.

This isn't even including the likes of Devin Vassell, Keldon Johnson, and the war chest of draft picks that should be in tow.

One potential downside for the Spurs is likely needing to part ways with draft assets to trade De'Aaron Fox away. While the trade for Fox made since at the time, Harper's emergence opens the door to fully commit to him long-term. The contract Fox is in control of will be difficult to move without attaching draft capital in all likelihood.

Center Luke Kornet is a win-now mode, as well as forwards Harrison Barnes and Tobias Harris. These players give San Antonio value in the moment without sacrificing future flexibility.

GettyStephon Castle is the perfect third star for San Antonio.

Oklahoma City is nearly as flush with controllable assets as San Antonio is, which sets the stage for a heavyweight battle for years to come.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is entering the season as the consensus top player in the league. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren are both high-level stars and potential trade chips. Oklahoma City's trade asset chest is on-par with the Spurs' as well. San Antonio head coach Mitch Johnson is one of the brightest rising minds in the NBA. Oklahoma City head coach Mark Daigneault is already a champion, while setting the stage for even more growth.

The two franchises – in many ways – mirror one another. While San Antonio is a safe bet to be the best team in the league in three years, Oklahoma City has just as strong of a case. This is especially driven by the Thunder's ability to draft, which is fueled by GM Sam Presti's astute nature.

The playoff series in May simply served as a prelude for what is to come.

title: Hartford Wolf Pack celebrating 30th season in CT with promotion-filled schedule
description: As the Hartford Wolf Pack hockey club begins its 30th season in Hartford, fans of the franchise are in for more than just one treat.  The team moved to Hartford ahead of the 1997-98 season, competing in the American Hockey League, which it still does today.  During that entire stretch, the franchise played in the same downtown arena, formerly known as the Hartford Civic Center and then XL Center, before becoming PeoplesBank Arena last year.
fullText:
As the Hartford Wolf Pack hockey club begins its 30th season in Hartford, fans of the franchise are in for more than just one treat.

The New York Rangers' top minor-league affiliate has scheduled a season full of fun promotions to commemorate three decades in Connecticut's capital city.

The team moved to Hartford ahead of the 1997-98 season, competing in the American Hockey League, which it still does today.

During that entire stretch, the franchise played in the same downtown arena, formerly known as the Hartford Civic Center and then XL Center, before becoming PeoplesBank Arena last year. That building remains its home.

Like the arena, the team hasn't been immune to name changes.

After taking the ice as the Wolf Pack from 1997 to 2010, the franchise changed its name to the Connecticut Whale. The name change paid homage to the Hartford Whalers, the city's former National Hockey League team.

Despite the nostalgia, fans demanded the team restore the Wolf Pack brand, which it did following the 2012-2013 season.

Entering the 2013-2014 campaign, the Wolf Pack name returned, and it has persevered until the present day.

To celebrate that tradition, the team's promotional schedule this season includes a variety of exciting giveaways.

The home slate begins on Saturday, Oct. 10, against the Wilkes-Barre-Scranton Penguins. That evening, fans are encouraged to wear white.

White T-shirts will cover the arena's lower bowl seats that evening thanks to Pepsi.

The following day, Sunday, Oct. 11, features a match against the Laval Rocket at 3 p.m. in Hartford. Thanks to Pepsi, the first 2,500 fans to enter the arena will get a magnetic schedule.

Other giveaways include a Sonar bobblehead hand-out on Jan. 15, a Wolf Pack branded trucker hat giveaway on Jan. 22, a 'best friends bobblehead' giveaway on Jan. 23, a Wolf Pack branded basketball jersey giveaway on March 13, and a Wolf Pack branded captain's hat on March 19.

On Friday nights, all season long through the first intermission at PeoplesBank Arena, there will be $3 drafts and $3 hot dogs available.

The CTDOT Family Value Pack is also returning for another season and will be available on Oct. 11, Nov. 27, Dec. 11, March 14 and April 9.

Over the course of next season, the Wolf Pack will wear three specialty jerseys.

The first jersey will be worn as part of the team's "Hockey Fights Cancer" festivities on Nov. 14.

Meanwhile, "Emo Night" jerseys will be reintroduced Jan. 15 on "Emo Night," and on March 6, the Wolf Pack will wear a special "30th Anniversary jersey" to honor its past in Hartford.

Jersey designs and details will be released later.

Postgame events with Wolf Pack players will return this year, and a date will be released later.

"Hockey Happy Hour" also returns.

Presented by Minuteman Press Hartford, the happy hour takes place prior to all Friday and Saturday home Wolf Pack games in the Chill Zone two hours before the puck drops.

Patrons can buy a $18 wristband to receive access to the expanded Fan Fare buffet and $3, 12-0z domestic draft beers until the start of the game.

The full list of the Hartford Wolf Pack's promotions this season can be seen here.

title: Bulls Legend Reveals What It Will Take To Return To Glory
description: The Chicago Bulls finally feel like they’re moving in the right direction after embracing a full-scale rebuild over the past 12 months.However, part of being a rebuilding team is remaining patient as the young talent on the roster develops and finds their roles in the league. Of course, that sounds easy in practice, but the […] The post Bulls Legend Reveals What It Will Take To Return To Glory appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Chicago Bulls finally feel like they're moving in the right direction after embracing a full-scale rebuild over the past 12 months.

However, part of being a rebuilding team is remaining patient as the young talent on the roster develops and finds their roles in the league. Of course, that sounds easy in practice, but the process can take multiple years, and sometimes, teams get impatient.

During a recent conversation with Kyle Odegard of Action Network, former Bulls champion Horace Grant urged the team to remain patient with the franchise's new young core.

"To go back iconic like we did back in the day, it's going to take some work," Grant said. "It's going to take some patience. But with the core they have now, staying healthy, and then I still think they need a little bit more leadership in that locker room. I played with some great leaders in Chicago. MJ, Pip, Bill Cartwright, you can throw John Paxson in there as well."

"The city is going to have to stay patient, because they are a very young crew," Grant said. "I tell people this: when Scottie and I first got there in '87, we were getting our heads knocked in by the Detroit Pistons almost every year. It took patience. It took trust in each other, and then the rest is history."

Chicago's new young core has the potential to take the team back toward the top of the Eastern Conference. However, the path isn't going to be easy, and moves will need to be made along the way. Still, right now, the fanbase will undoubtedly be excited about what's to come.

During his conversation with Action Network, Grant also shared his thoughts on Caleb Wilson, who the Bulls selected with the fourth-overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

"Oh my goodness, man," Grant said. "What a beast. What a freakin' beast. He has all the intangibles, the skill set. But what I love about him is that he has the mindset of a killer. A dog. He goes out and gets it."

Granted continued, noting how Wilson is one of Chicago's best draft picks since the addition of Derrick Rose.

"It's one of the best draft picks since Derrick Rose. I'm not going to put him with MJ and myself and Pip, but since Derrick Rose, one of the greatest choices the Bulls have made, in my humble opinion."

Wilson undoubtedly has superstar potential. However, he'll need to navigate his rookie season and continue improving long-term in order to reach his ceiling.

Grant also noted that his nephew, Jerami Grant, was impressed by new Bulls head coach, Tiago Splitter last season.

"I haven't talked to (Splitter) as of yet," Grant said. "I'm pretty sure he's still trying to get pieces around him, as far as assistant coaches, player development guys. But the craziest thing is he coached my nephew down in Portland."

Chicago is well position to develop into a genuine force in the coming years. However, in order for that to happen, everyone needs to be on the same page and remain patient.

title: Why Klay Thompson chose to sign with Heat, Coach Erik Spoelstra amid NBA offseason suitors
description: Klay Thompson had a very specific reason for choosing the Heat led by Coach Erik Spoelstra and Giannis Antetokounmpo.
fullText:
Why Klay Thompson chose to sign with Heat, Coach Erik Spoelstra amid NBA offseason suitors originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

When an NBA player reaches the twilight of their career, they know it, and an instinct to go after the Larry O'Brien trophy kicks in. Klay Thompson feels that exact feeling right now. After two seasons with the Dallas Mavericks, he decided to join forces with the Miami Heat led by Giannis Antetokounmpo and Coach Erik Spoelstra. Why exactly did he make that call? It all came down to adding another ring to his resume.

It is no secret that Klay Thompson found his perfect match with the Heat. When Giannis Antetokounmpo is on the floor, teams typically build a wall to prevent him from scoring in the paint. How does Coach Erik Spoelstra solve this problem? Shooters.

The Heat are no stranger to this conundrum. Coach Spoelstra experienced the same situation with LeBron James. Back then, they got Shane Battier, Mike Miller, Mario Chalmers, James Jones and Ray Allen. Now, they'll do the same with Antetokounmpo after Thompson arrives.

This schematic and rotation fit makes so much sense for the Heat. In fact, Thompson posits that his aim really is to hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy once again. If it means he has to play that specific role for Coach Spoelstra and Antetokounmpo, he would gladly do it.

He even outlined other reasons for joining the Heat in his introductory press conference.

"Just the opportunity to play high-level basketball throughout the season and the chance to make a deep postseason run. Those things were so attractive to me. Obviously, you want to maximize your potential as an athlete. I've tasted winning before; there's really nothing like it. Even just getting there and failing is better than not having a shot at it... Looking at the roster, it looked like a great fit as far as me being able to space the floor," Thompson declared.

Thompson couldn't compete to his full potential after the Warriors' 2022 NBA Championship run. Stephen Curry and the Warriors couldn't make it over the hump again, despite certain acquisitions. When he moved to the Mavericks, they tanked for Cooper Flagg in one season. During his last run with them, it was also clear it was a developmental year to define their identity.

This time around, Thompson will be surrounded by other veteran stars who have been craving a Larry O'Brien trophy. All he has to do is start knocking down shots, spacing the floor, and playing tighter defense if he wants that fifth ring to land on his finger come 2027. Can he help the Heat while breaking out of his shell?

title: Sky Owner Announced Enes Kanter Decision After Altercation
description: The Chicago Sky found themselves in the middle of a news cycle involving one of their players and former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom.During the second half of the Sky’s 113-90 loss to the Indiana Fever, Sky guard Natasha Cloud got into a verbal altercation with Kanter, who was sitting courtside with a shirt reading […] The post Sky Owner Announced Enes Kanter Decision After Altercation appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Chicago Sky found themselves in the middle of a news cycle involving one of their players and former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom.

During the second half of the Sky's 113-90 loss to the Indiana Fever, Sky guard Natasha Cloud got into a verbal altercation with Kanter, who was sitting courtside with a shirt reading "WOMAN noun. adult human female." Security at Wintrust Arena then escorted Kanter from the game.

Kanter has since posted on social media and appeared on television defending himself. A new perspective is being told by the owner of the Sky.

GettyCHICAGO, ILLINOIS – AUGUST 23: Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom looks on during the second half between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on August 23, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images)

Sky owner Michael Alter met with the local media on Tuesday to discuss the incident. According to Front Office Sports' Colin Salao, Kanter's manager texted Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca that Kanter was coming to the game. Alter said that Pagliocca has not talked to Kanter in "three or four years."

Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter is meeting with local Chicago Sky beat writers and local Chicago media.

— Colin Salao (@colincsalao) August 25, 2026

After that, Alter made it clear that Kanter's intentions were to be "provocative and just see how much attention he could get," but added he did not know where he was sitting before the game. Alter even spoke to people who were sitting near him to get the story.

"They each confirmed that the dialogue between Cloud and Kanter started with Kanter. He began to chirp with her sometime in the third quarter. I would characterize it as trash talking, nothing personal. Basketball-related, but enough to get her attention and to engage her, and in my opinion, to try to provoke her."

"He portrays as this victimless person who did nothing, said nothing. Just wearing a t-shirt … We have five different security authorities that all agreed very quickly to throw him out because he made himself into a threat."

Alter announced that Kanter will no longer be allowed at Wintrust Arena "unless sometime in the future, he's able to prove to us that he's able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat." Alter's only regret is that he didn't tell the Sky players before the game, since it was close to tipoff.

GettyAmerican basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom poses during an interview with AFP at the United Nations Office in Geneva on April 5, 2022. Enes Kanter Freedom, whose human rights advocacy has ruffled feathers, hopes to bend UN human rights chief Michelle Bachelet's ear on Thursday about her forthcoming China visit. (Photo by Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP via Getty Images)

This follows conversations about transgender women in sports, first raised by Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. Kanter and other former NBA players joined the conversation by saying they were "declaring" for the 2027 WNBA Draft. The league has since said he and the other players are not eligible.

No other WNBA teams have announced whether they will take action on it. As of the release of this article, Kanter did not respond to the news.

The Chicago Sky are back in action Tuesday to face the Connecticut Sun. They will then face the New York Liberty on Saturday before entering the World Cup break.

fullText:
UFC BMF champion Charles Oliveira called for a rematch against Justin Gaethje, with both the BMF and lightweight titles on the line.

Oliveira defeated Gaethje in the main event of UFC 274 in May 2022 in a fight in which Oliveira, who was the UFC lightweight champion at the time, missed weight on the scale.

During the fight, Gaethje knocked the Brazilian down early on in the bout, but Oliveira regained his composure and was able to submit Gaethje soon thereafter after scoring. knockdown of his own.

Now, four years later, Oliveira is calling for the two to fight again, this time with Gaethje as the champion and Oliveira chasing his belt.

Speaking to Brazilian MMA reporter Olhar da Luta, Oliveira made it clear that he wants Gaethje next with both the BMF and UFC lightweight titles on the line.

"With all due respect, I'm not looking backward. I'm looking forward. I want to fight for the title. That's what I'm focused on. The UFC likes a story… I was robbed (in our first fight). They wanted to distract me so I would go in there, have an (expletive) fight, and they could crown him champion. He felt my hands, I dropped him and then I submitted him. There's a story there. And now he's the champion. I have no problem with that. The rematch doesn't need to be in Brazil. Just like I went to his home turf before, it can be in his backyard, it can be in Las Vegas, on the street corner, in Japan, anywhere in the world. I just need one phone call telling me the date and time. So if the UFC wants a story, what bigger story is there than that?" Oliveira said.

Charles Oliveira just called out Justin Gaethje for a rematch ð

"With all due respect, I'm not looking backward. I'm looking forward. I want to fight for the title. That's what I'm focused on.

The UFC likes a story… I was robbed [in our first fight]. They wanted to distractâ¦ pic.twitter.com/tfrd45hEzl

— Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) August 25, 2026

While Oliveira vs. Gaethje is a fine rematch, it's hard to say that Oliveira deserves the title shot more than the winner of the UFC 331 co-main event between Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy, a fight that seems like a No. 1 contender bout.

Oliveira was actually slated to fight Tsarukyan originally on this card, but after his long-time teammate Allan Nascimento passed away, Oliveira was forced to withdraw from the bout, which is understandable.

We'll see what the UFC ultimately decides to do, but there is no doubt a rematch between Oliveira and Gaethje would be fun for the fans to watch.

title: Jeff Passan Rejects Conspiracy Theories of ‘Financial Fraud’ by Dodgers
description: Jeff Passan wasn't having it when a social media user questioned his coverage of the Dodgers.
fullText:
An ESPN insider is speaking out against online theories that a reported federal probe into the owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers indicate wrongdoing by the team.

Jeff Passan sounded off on X, formerly Twitter, regarding the investigation into Mark Walter, the majority owner of the Boys in Blue who recently agreed to sell his Lakers ownership.

As Passan noted, the federal probe is into Walter's other businesses, and there's nothing to connect the Dodgers except the common ownership by Walter and his companies, Guggenheim Partners and TWG Global.

"I have no evidence — and no other media member has reported any — that the Dodgers did anything that ran afoul of the [collective bargaining agreement]," Passan responded to a user who critiqued his reporting. "Beyond that, the government is focused more on procedural questions — the mismarking of affiliated investments and the web of companies under Guggenheim's umbrella — than anything specifically related to the Dodgers."

That user took issue with what Passan called "the full story that helps separate fact from fiction" and suggested that the reporter "acknowledge your own naivete in declaring that the Dodgers 'cracked the system.'"

"That was the phrase that had most of baseball twitter roasting you," they wrote. "All you had to say was financial fraud does not equal cracking the system, but alas, your ego got in the way."

"You are well within your rights to assume whatever you want to assume, and if you want to suggest there was some kind of fraud that specifically impacted on-field performance, you do you," he wrote. "I'm not going to do that because I have no idea how the money they received from selling the debt on their TV network, for example, was used. I wasn't being naive when I said the Dodgers cracked the system. They did."

Passan detailed that the Dodgers "recognized that cash is a grand separator in terms of securing talent," but that's not all it takes to win.

"You know who else did? The Mets. And they stunk. Every billionaire has access to cash. Not as much as the Dodgers, certainly, but if they want to get more capital to invest in their team, they can. They choose not to," Passan said. "And that is well within their rights, too, but to suggest that because Mark Walter is under investigation for one business' tactics that it automatically ties into another's — with zero hard evidence showing that's the case — is simply a case of you fitting what you think you know to a conclusion you already made."

title: Philadelphia Eagles’ QB Battle Gets Intriguing Update After Patriots Game
description: The Philadelphia Eagles‘ QB2 battle is under a microscope this offseason, as the team has struggled to pick between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee. fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles' QB2 battle is under a microscope this offseason, as the team has struggled to pick between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee.

After a Week 2 loss against the New England Patriots in the NFL preseason, there just might be a bit of a breakthrough.

When the Eagles linked for practice on Monday, August 24, Tanner McKee was utilized as the first Jalen Hurts backup, a position that Dalton has held for most of the offseason.

GettyFOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS – AUGUST 22: Andy Dalton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on in the first quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles during a preseason game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)

"Tanner McKee was first up as QB2 today," Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation wrote on Monday.

"Nothing overly flashy but a lot of shorter completions. Felt like the ball rarely hit the ground when he was out there. Andy Dalton did have a good completion to Moore along the sideline. No major movement in this battle today."

GettyBALTIMORE, MD – AUGUST 15: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles hands the ball off to Will Shipley #28 during the first half of the preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images)

Before the first week of the preseason, Dalton seemed to be in front. He was picking up most of the QB2 reps. After Game 1 in Baltimore, there wasn't any movement. Both quarterbacks struggled within the offense.

Week 2 was a different story. Dalton struggled as the starter against the New England Patriots. McKee came in and thrived.

After the game, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni claimed that the battle was still ongoing, but there seems to be a little more intrigue with McKee at QB2 this week.

GettyPHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – JANUARY 04: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles warm ups prior to the game against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images)

âThe reason Andy is going in first is because heâs not going to play as much as Tanner because he has more experience and he has more experience within this type of system, and Tanner needs to continue to play there,â Sirianni said after the game.

âI think you saw the improvements there from Tanner. We got to continue to give both of them opportunities within practice and potentially games. Weâll see how both games go. Obviously, Iâm not there yet [for next weekâs game]. But obviously, that was the plan today.â

The Eagles will close out their preseason on Friday against the Cincinnati Bengals. It seems there is a chance that McKee could get the starting nod.

title: Kyle Shanahan: Jed York's arrest "has no effect on us"
description: Shanahan insists owners legal issue won't be a distraction.
fullText:
It's been a bizarre couple of months for the 49ers, with the most bizarre development happening on Monday, when team owner Jed York pleaded no contest to a pair of charges arising from an effort to solicit prostitution.

Coach Kyle Shanahan was asked about the situation by reporters on Tuesday.

"I got to talk to Jed the last two days and today," Shanahan said. "Obviously, it's a very tough situation. I mean, views for the organization going forward is the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that, but I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I've got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle [York]. Their family does mean a lot to me. So, with it being this personal, I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way."

Shanahan added that the situation is "irrelevant" to players, especially since York has been living in Ohio and absent from training camp.

"From a football standpoint, it has no effect on us," Shanahan said. "As far as what we do day-to-day, what we talk about. It hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today, it doesn't have to do with what happens on the field. Everything outside of there, I think you guys can judge that better than me."

He insists that the York arrest won't be a distraction.

"Well, the one thing that went on yesterday, I don't think pertained to our players much," Shanahan said. "And if you guys talk about me getting in a car accident, I think that's kind of a joke that people think that's a distraction to our team. So, I think it's been training camp as usual."

Right, but it's one thing for an absentee owner to get arrested. It surely was a distraction, and a disruption, for the 49ers to not have Shanahan at full capacity in the early stages of training camp.

As to York, the fact that Shanahan was asked several questions about it on Tuesday necessarily makes it a distraction. Even if there's no reason to believe it will be a disruption.

title: Knightsbridge pulls away to win the $1M Pacific Classic by 6 1/4 lengths
description: Knightsbridge won the $1 million Pacific Classic at Del Mar, pulling away by 6 1/4 lengths. Ridden by Junior Alvarado, the 5-year-old horse ran 1 1/4 miles in 2:01.79.
fullText:
DEL MAR, Calif. (AP) — Knightsbridge withstood a fierce battle on the lead in the early going before pulling away to win the $1 million Pacific Classic by 6 1/4 lengths at Del Mar on Saturday.

Ridden by Junior Alvarado, Knightsbridge ran 1 1/4 miles in 2:01.79. The 5-year-old horse had shipped to the seaside track north of San Diego from the East Coast after a win in the Monmouth Cup five weeks ago in New Jersey.

"He was kind of skipping over the ground," Alvarado said. "I had my hopes that when I asked him he would give me his best right when we turned for home. It was all heart there. He's a horse that has a lot of talent."

Knightsbridge was challenged over the opening mile by the speedy Full Serrano before shaking him off at the head of the stretch. The winner paid $4.20 as the wagering favorite.

Original Sin finished second. Full Serrano was another 1 1/2 lengths back in third in the West Coast's richest race.

The victory, worth $600,000, increased Knightsbridge's career earnings to $1,523,155, with eight wins in 12 starts. He earned a berth in the $7 million Breeders' Cup Classic at Keeneland in October.

It was Hall of Fame trainer Bill Mott's second Pacific Classic win, having taken the 2008 edition with Go Between.

Knightsbridge is owned and bred by Godolphin, founded by Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoun.

title: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez weighs in on lingering contract situation
description: Tuesday marked the final, official training camp practice, and the Patriots’ star cornerback is still waiting on a new deal.
fullText:
Tuesday marked the final, official training camp practice, and the Patriots' star cornerback is still waiting on a new deal.

Christian Gonzalez spoke to the media Tuesday and kept many details of the negotiations close to the vest.

Boston 25's Lauren Walsh asked Gonzalez what he feels he's worth in this new deal he's seeking.

"The office knows how I feel," Gonzalez said. "My team has made it known what I feel I'm worth, so the right people know what I'm worth."

I asked Christian Gonzalez what he thinks he’s worth in terms of this new contract.

Gonzalez: “The office knows how I feel. My team has made it known what I feel I’m worth, so the right people know what I’m worth.”#Patriots #NEPats @boston25 pic.twitter.com/xQA50UnOX6

Gonzalez is one of the top cornerbacks in the NFL, and the market rate for the league's best corners was recently raised when Seattle signed Devon Witherspoon to a $132 million extension with more than $101 million in guaranteed money and an average yearly value of $33 million.

Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf also spoke to the media and fielded many questions about Gonzalez.

Wolf confirmed that the contract the Patriots have offered Gonzalez would still make him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. That was a significant affirmation, because team owner Robert Kraft stated that on the opening day of training camp, and since then, multiple cornerbacks have signed new deals with each raising the market rate for the top players at that position.

"Nothing new to report on Christian," Wolf said. "We want him here. He's an elite player. I've been on record saying that before, and we're continuing to work with his representation to find a resolution that works for everyone."

Gonzalez also did not share details of the negotiations with the Patriots.

"I can't really get into it," Gonzalez said. "I've said I want to keep it between my team and the Patriots and it's been out there, so it is what it is. Can't really go back in time, so just got to focus on right now."

Wolf commended Gonzalez's participation in camp throughout the negotiations, and his recent return from injury.

"He's been great," Wolf said. "He came back yesterday and looked like he hadn't missed a beat. He had some productive one-on-one reps, and then he was making plays in the red zone. So again, he's a competitor, he's talented, he's elite. And again, hopefully we can get something done there."

Asked if Gonzalez's recent absence missing two weeks of training camp was entirely injury-related or if it was contract related, Gonzalez said, "I'm not going to get into that. I'm out here now, so it is what it is."

Gonzalez admitted frustration as the negotiations have dragged on for the entirety of training camp without a signed deal.

"I mean it's frustrating, but I mean, I'm focused on the season," Gonzalez said. "I'm focused on here now and doing what I got to do. I'm out here to compete and get better."

The Patriots open the season against the Seattle Seahawks on the road Wednesday, September 9.

title: PGA chief says 'no current plans' for LIV stars to return
description: The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive officer Brian Rolapp said Tuesday. While the PGA Tour offered a temporary path back for some LIV players --  five-time major winner Brooks Koepka in January took advantage, paying financial penalties -- no repeats are planned, said Rolapp.
fullText:
The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive officer Brian Rolapp said Tuesday.

Launched in 2022, LIV caused shockwaves in the golf world as it spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the traditional PGA, but its survival is now deeply uncetain.

Having lost their Saudi investors, LIV organizers have promised a slimmed-down "2.0" version next year with new investors, but several key players have been linked with exits.

While the PGA Tour offered a temporary path back for some LIV players --  five-time major winner Brooks Koepka in January took advantage, paying financial penalties -- no repeats are planned, said Rolapp.

"Currently there's no current plans for Returning Member Program like you saw earlier this year," he said, ahead of this week's season-ending Tour Championship in Atlanta, Georgia.

The PGA has banned LIV players from its events, insisting any player wishing to return must first entirely cut ties with LIV, and Rolapp told Tuesday's press conference that "rules matter."

"Accountability and discipline are essential to any organization, and certainly for the integrity of the TOUR and for the game," he said.

Rolapp said it was impossible to speculate on if and how other LIV players could one day return to the PGA because "I don't know the future of LIV."

"We've been consistent. Anyone who's interested in coming to the PGA TOUR needs to demonstrate that they are relieved of their contractual commitments or any tail obligations they might have in that legacy model," he said.

"Brooks certainly did that, and until then, we weren't really able to consider anything seriously. I would say the same thing here."

LIV organizers have vowed to return next year with a slimmed-down schedule, smaller prizes and new investors.

Speaking at LIV's season-ending Indianapolis event Sunday, DeChambeau said he was "proud" of what the tour has achieved, and said he had "great thoughts about what could happen next year."

But on Monday he published an enigmatic post on Instagram -- photos of several LIV victories, with the caption "It was a good run."

title: Golf giant Callaway apologizes after ad sparks outcry
description: Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver.The online advert showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark barging Epson Tour professional player Alexis Miestowski to the ground when she attempts to reach for his driver, before warning her: "Do not touch my new driver."
fullText:
Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver.

The commercial, which was released online last week before being pulled, triggered a backlash over its depiction of violence against women, in addition to calls for a boycott of Callaway products.

Callaway golf chief executive Chip Brewer said in a statement on Tuesday that the company had launched an investigation into how the advert -- produced by golf media firm Good Good Golf -- had been approved.

"Last week Good Good Golf and Callaway posted a video to promote a co-branded driver," Brewer said in a statement.

"While the video was produced by Good Good, it was approved by Callaway prior to posting. That approval should never have happened. Mistakes were made and we are taking the matter very seriously.

"As we deal with the consequences of our mistake and complete our investigations, I want to make it clear that we sincerely apologize for the video.

"The content was inappropriate and does not reflect our values. To be clear: we are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence or threatening behavior of any kind... I assure you we will learn from this and do better."

The online advert showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark barging Epson Tour professional player Alexis Miestowski to the ground when she attempts to reach for his driver, before warning her: "Do not touch my new driver."

Good Good Golf, which centers its business around a successful YouTube channel aimed at bringing a younger audience to the sport, had already apologized for the controversial advert.

"We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand," Good Good said in a statement.

"We have since taken that content down. And sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward."

Good Good's rise will see the company be the title sponsor for the PGA Tour's inaugural Good Good Championship in Austin, Texas in November.

PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp said on Tuesday the circuit was dismayed by the advert and Good Good's handling of the controversy.

"I think what we saw was concerning, is clearly not aligned with PGA TOUR values. We take it very seriously," Rolapp said.

"I think their initial response was disappointing. It was a bit defensive and late.

"But I think the responses are getting better. I think we've seen some things this morning, we've had some conversations with them, so we'll continue to monitor and work with them going forward. But no, we were disappointed with what we saw."

fullText:
SPRINGFIELD, Mo. — The Springfield Cardinals will soon have a new name.

The organization announced Tuesday that it will rebrand following the 2026 Minor League Baseball season, ending more than two decades under the Springfield Cardinals name.

Beginning in 2026, the team will have a new name, logos and uniforms. The franchise will remain in Springfield, continue playing at Route 66 Stadium and remain the Double-A affiliate of the St. Louis Cardinals.

The new identity has already been selected, according to the team, but fans will have to wait a little longer to find out what it is.

The organization plans to unveil the new name, logos and uniforms during a free launch party at Route 66 Stadium on Tuesday, Oct. 6. Additional details will be announced later.

The Springfield Cardinals have played in the city since 2005. The organization said the change intended to give the team an identity more closely connected to Springfield and southwest Missouri.

title: Olympic hero Alysa Liu to sit out figure skating season before 2027 return
description: Olympic champion Alysa Liu will sit out the 2026-27 figure skating season, taking another break from competition while continuing to train ahead of a planned return the following year.  “I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry and skating can evolve,” Liu wrote.  Liu told NBC Sports that she intends to continue working with her longtime Bay Area coaches, Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali, with an emphasis on her “overall artistry, spins, jumps, everything”.
fullText:
Olympic champion Alysa Liu will sit out the 2026-27 figure skating season, taking another break from competition while continuing to train ahead of a planned return the following year.

The 21-year-old American announced her decision on social media, saying she wanted time to "recalibrate" and develop her skating away from the demands of competition.

"I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry and skating can evolve," Liu wrote. "It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth."

Liu told NBC Sports that she intends to continue working with her longtime Bay Area coaches, Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali, with an emphasis on her "overall artistry, spins, jumps, everything".

"I really want to improve my skating, and I wanted to take the time to do that for myself and just to evolve," she said. "And then I'll be back after that is done."

The decision represents another unconventional turn in a career that has carried Liu from child prodigy to burnout, retirement and an unlikely return as world and Olympic champion.

Liu became the youngest ever US women's champion aged 13, when her 4ft 6in frame left her too short to reach the top of the podium without help from the other medalists. But the relentless training and attention that accompanied her rapid ascent gradually drained her enthusiasm for the sport.

She retired at 16, only months after finishing sixth in her Olympic debut at the 2022 Beijing Games, and later described how comprehensively she had come to reject the life built around her skating.

"I really hated skating when I quit," Liu said in the run-up to the Milano Cortina Olympics. "I didn't care about competitions. I didn't care about places. I didn't care about skaters. I didn't care about my programs. I just wanted to get away."

Liu enrolled at UCLA, studied psychology and went hiking in the Himalayas with friends while discovering an identity beyond the rink. Her desire to skate returned unexpectedly during a ski trip to Lake Tahoe, where gliding down the mountain rekindled her love of movement.

She began skating once a week at public sessions in El Segundo, California, and found that the difficult jumps that had propelled her childhood rise had not entirely deserted her. Liu eventually decided to mount a comeback, but only with greater control over her career, including her music, costumes, diet and training schedule.

The results would no longer define the experience, she insisted. Her initial ambition was simply to make another Olympic team and use the sport as a form of self-expression.

That approach carried Liu to a surprise world championship in 2025, making her the first American woman to win the title since Kimmie Meissner in 2006. In February, she landed seven clean triple jumps to rise from third place after the short program and win the Olympic women's singles title in Milan.

The West Oakland native became the first American woman to claim the event since Sarah Hughes in 2002. She also won gold in the Olympic team competition.

"Really the only word that comes to mind when I think about my entire journey is grateful," Liu told NBC Sports. "I think the reason why it's been so fun is because I have my own agency. I really like to skate, and so that's why I skate."

Liu said she assessed her emotional and physical state earlier this summer and concluded that stepping away was the right choice. DiGuglielmo and Scali supported the decision.

"Logically and emotionally and physically, this just makes the most sense," she told NBC Sports. "I will miss seeing the international competitors at all the international competitions, but there will be more, so it's fine."

A rush of opportunities followed Liu's Olympic victory. Nearly 5,000 people turned out for a homecoming celebration in her honor, where Oakland mayor Barbara Lee presented her with a key to the city. She withdrew from the world championships in March, performed alongside her Olympic teammates on the Stars on Ice tour, attended Louis Vuitton's Paris Fashion Week show and wore the label to the Met Gala.

Liu had been scheduled to compete at Skate America from 13-15 November in Everett, Washington.

title: Klay Thompson points to 'redemption season' in Miami
description: "The opportunity to win again at a very high level was so attractive to me."
fullText:
One doesn't have to look too hard on social media to find someone using the word "washed" in the same sentence as Klay Thompson's name.

Which is exactly why the four-time champion and future Hall of Famer wanted to join the Heat, Thompson said at his introductory press conference, via the Associated Press.

"It's kind of a redemption season for me to show I can still make an impact on winning and do it consistently," Thompson said. "I can't wait to get to work. It's pretty surreal being here. But what an honor it is....

"I've tasted winning before and there's really nothing like it. The opportunity to win again at a very high level was so attractive to me."

Thompson put his money where his mouth was about winning, giving up more than $9 million of his $17.5 million contract to facilitate a buyout in Dallas. Then he signed with the Heat for two years, $11.5 million (more total money, less per year), making about $5.6 million this season (low enough that the Heat can fill out their roster with two veteran minimum contracts).

Thompson got into more detail about what he wants sitting down with Brendan Tobin.

"I just missed out on the postseason [last season with the Warriors]. I hate watching from home. You get FOMO watching all your coworkers just getting to chase their dreams and it's not fun not making the playoffs. That's all I want to do these next couple years. Have a chance to make a deep postseason run. So excited to be in Miami. They're a very demanding organization, but I love being in that ultra-competitive atmosphere, and this was a match made in heaven."

Thompson should get his chance to compete in the postseason this season. He is expected to start in Miami, a team that has worked to put as much shooting as possible around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. Last season, Thompson averaged a career-low 11.7 points a game but shot 38.3% from 3-point range on a healthy 7.6 attempts per game — he should thrive in the up-tempo offense expected from the Heat. Expect him to hit a lot of trail and corner 3-pointers in transition.

The opportunities will be there for Thompson to prove all his detractors wrong, to get his redemption. He just has to grab them.

title: O'Neill takes responsibility with nowhere to hide for Celtic
description: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill says his team have a "million miles to go" after defeat in Austria.
fullText:
In the open air of the Raiffeisen Arena, with bedlam all around, there was nowhere to hide for Celtic or Martin O'Neill.

The Scottish champions had endured one of the darkest nights in their European history.

After going out to Kairat Almaty on penalties last year at this stage of the Champions League play-offs, that is saying something.

Four goals up on aggregate against LASK, O'Neill's Celtic somehow conspired to implode in a second half with little sign of a response on the way to a 5-4 aggregate loss following extra time.

There was no hiding place, and the Celtic manager was frank when put in the spotlight at full-time.

"I'm responsible for this one," he said.

"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the Uefa Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.

"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

Celtic blow four-goal lead to LASK in Champions League collapse

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded

O'Neill was not in charge for that defeat in Kazakhstan a year ago as it triggered the start of the end for Brendan Rodgers' second spell at Celtic Park.

The current Parkhead boss helped steady Celtic's ship last term following Rodgers' exit and again following the Wilfried Nancy saga to guide them to another league title and a Scottish Cup.

This season appeared to get off to a prosperous start until the roof began to cave in over in Austria.

Away from the raw pain of stumbling in such a stark way, the aftermath could be telling for Celtic who now have to not only pick themselves up, but finish off a transfer window without the hefty windfall which would have blown in with the Champions League.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said O'Neill.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."

Celtic captain Callum McGregor tells Amazon Prime: "We got what we deserved. We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere.

"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.

"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, you can't have any excuse and that's on us.

"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions [on whether the squad are ready] are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere.

"This is what it's like to play at Celtic. You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown on BBC Radio Scotland: "It was a fantastic start, you go 1-0 up, but that seems like forever ago. Now they've crashed out the Champions League and conceded five goals.

"LASK outran Celtic in a couple of areas, the two up front were strong, solid and willing runners.

"LASK deserve to go through with that performance. I feel for the lads because I've been in that situation as well."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Amazon Prime: "It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted. Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

Former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov: "Everyone [is to blame].

"They are all in it together. A big club like Celtic should be able to hold that out."

title: Bears Camp Report: Darnell Wright injured, Corners return, Jordan van den Berg with the ones, and more
description: There was a lot going on at the Bears practice at Halas Hall today. @wiltfongjr shares some news here.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears held their final training camp practice in front of the fans today at Halas Hall, and before they got into a red zone period, cornerback Jaylon Johnson brought the team together for a meeting with the message that the practice wasn't good enough. The message was heard as tight end Cole Kmet said in his post-practice presser, "I thought it ended up being one of our better practices through camp so far."

A strong finish for the nearly 2-hour practice before what will likely be a light workout tomorrow and a joint practice with the Tennessee Titans on Thursday. The Bears play the Titans to close the preseason slate on Saturday.

The Bears could be without a few players the rest of the week, as several left today with an injury, most notably starting right tackle Darnell Wright, who exited to Halas Hall with trainers as he flexed his right arm. That's the same arm he injured last season, so hopefully there's good news coming about that.

Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. also left with an injury, and in case you missed it, he was at the center of a trade rumor today. Tight end Hayden Large was sidelined with a left arm issue, and cornerback Dontae Manning also left practice and did not return.

Running back Kyle Monangai is still week-to-week, new defensive end Marcus Davenport wasn't practicing, and defensive end Austin Booker, who missed Saturday's game in Cincinnati, was also not participating.

However, the Bears did get some good news on the injury front. Safety Elijah Hicks and rookie linebacker Keyshaun Elliott were activated from the PUP list, and both got in some work. Quarterback Tyson Bagent returned after missing last week with a hamstring issue. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson was back in team drills, starting along with Jaylon Johnson. Backup corners Terell Smith and Jaylon Jones were also back, but neither did team drills. Left tackle Ozzy Trapilo was suited up but still just doing individual drills.

A few other nuggets from the day.

Rookie DT Jordan van den Berg was working some with the starters.

With Booker not practicing, Jamree Kromah was getting some work with the ones. (link)

Defensive lineman James Lynch also spent time with the first team.

While head coach Ben Johnson said at his pre-practice press conference that they are still trying to figure out left tackle, Braxton Jones was with the ones most of the day. "From the angle I had, looked like LT Braxton Jones did a nice job in 9-on-7 period," shared Brad Biggs. "For the snaps he was in, there sure was an emphasis to run to his side. Three of the four D'Andre Swift runs went for nice gains."

Theo Benedet went in with the ones at right tackle with Wright out.

Cam Lewis got most of the work at safety next to rookie Dillon Thieneman. Ben Johnson said this morning that the safety spot next to the rookie is also an uncertainty.

Someone check the wind, because Zack Pearson shared that "Cairo Santos just drained a 59-yard field goal."

They closed practice with a long drive drill to test their cardio (link), and safety Xavier Woods ended practice by intercepting Case Keenum.

Per CHGO's Adam Hoge, defensive tackle Grady Jarrett yelled "Get up!" at d-linemen Jordan van den Berg and Montez Sweat when both were on a knee during the long drive drill.

From Michal Dwojak of Bears Insider:

Quarterback Caleb Williams and the first team offense had a mix of good and bad throughout the day. Williams moved the offense from its own 1 yard line when he found Rome Odunze down the middle for a big gain on third down. But Williams then completed one of his six pass attempts during a 7-on-7 drill — one of those were a drop by running back D'Andre Swift.

The first team offense had a good red zone period working from the defense's 14 yard line. Williams found Odunze once again for a touchdown pass before Swift ran in 14 yards for another touchdown on the following play.

Noah Sewell seems to be moving around really well. 

– cream pic.twitter.com/c0U7mf4s8V

Caleb rolls out, might be a sack in a live game but hits Loveland deep. 

– cream pic.twitter.com/DK71ClGAO2

Caleb completes to Raymond for gain of around 10. Nice grab. 

– cream pic.twitter.com/WcQc0oC8HP

Lettin' it fly 🎯 pic.twitter.com/X8RASDyPnR

title: Seahawks waive UDFA RB Anthony Hankerson
description: The Seahawks move on from Hankerson following the team’s second preseason matchup against the Titans.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks waived running back Anthony Hankerson on Monday, according to ESPN's Brady Henderson, prior to their final preseason matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Friday.

Hankerson rushed for 1,086 yards in 2025 at Oregon State prior to entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Miami Dolphins in May. He was waived by the Dolphins in August, before signing with the Seahawks during training camp.

The 22-year-old Hankerson rushed for 10 yards on five carries, and added nine receiving yards in the Seahawks' 19-16 loss to the Tennessee Titans in Week 2 of the preseason prior to being waived by Seattle.

The Seahawks move forward with a running back unit consisting of Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet, George Holani, Emanuel Wilson, Velus Jones Jr., and Jacardia Wright. Hankerson will be able to sign with another team as a free agent if he is not claimed off of waivers.

title: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw win PFA Player of the Year awards
description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City's Khadija Shaw won the women's award for the second time. Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.
fullText:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City's Khadija Shaw won the women's award for the second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.

He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."

The Portugal international is the Red Devils' first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009-10 and adds to his Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Manchester City sharpshooter Shaw, who was also recognized by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women's Player of the Year award for the second time.

The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again having scored 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and her maiden Women's Super League title.

Arsenal's Olivia Smith picked up the women's PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool and continued her form in the capital.

Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly was named men's PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze.

The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City team-mates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O'Reilly said: "I had a great season. I'm very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I'm over the moon how it turned out."

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford's Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by team-mates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa.

Mariona Caldentey, last year's PFA Women's Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo.

Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United's Jess Park were also included in a team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James.

Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football.

Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland's most capped player having represented his country on 102 occasions.

The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn's Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup.

Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

title: Kinley Rasmus breaks the record for hits by a girl at the Little League World Series
description: Kinley Rasmus is on a record-setting roll at the Little League World Series.  The 12-year-old pitcher and shortstop for the Phenix City, Alabama, team representing the Southeast at the tournament had a pair of hits during a comeback win over a team from Tacoma, Washington, on Tuesday that kept Phenix City's season alive.  Rasmus has five hits during the double-elimination tournament, the most by a girl at the Little League World Series.
fullText:
WILLIAMSPORT, Pa. (AP) — Kinley Rasmus is on a record-setting roll at the Little League World Series.

The 12-year-old pitcher and shortstop for the Phenix City, Alabama, team representing the Southeast at the tournament had a pair of hits during a comeback win over a team from Tacoma, Washington, on Tuesday that kept Phenix City's season alive.

Rasmus has five hits during the double-elimination tournament, the most by a girl at the Little League World Series.

The daughter of former major league pitcher Cory Rasmus has already distinguished herself on the mound. Kinley Rasmus allowed one hit in six innings in a game against Tacoma earlier in the tournament. The eight strikeouts she recorded in that outing tied Mo'Ne Davis' mark for strikeouts by a girl in a game.

Rasmus then added six more strikeouts in a victory on Monday to boost her tournament total to 14, also tying a record held by Davis.

She will have a chance to add to her hit total when Phenix City plays another elimination game on Wednesday.

title: Mike McCarthy open to keeping four quarterbacks
description: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy open to keeping four QBs.
fullText:
Mike McCarthy is not opposed to an unusually crowded quarterback room.

In fact, the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach believes keeping four quarterbacks could provide a meaningful benefit once the regular season begins, particularly given the depth and experience Pittsburgh has assembled at the position.

"I'd take six QBs in the building if it worked," McCarthy said via Mike DeFabo.

McCarthy's comments come as the Steelers evaluate their quarterback situation heading into the final stages of the preseason. Pittsburgh currently has four quarterbacks competing for roster spots: veteran Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, rookie Drew Allar and second-year quarterback Will Howard.

While most NFL teams typically carry three quarterbacks on their active roster, McCarthy indicated that the Steelers could consider keeping all four if the roster construction allows for it.

"If you have four quarterbacks in that room, especially given the quality that we have, I think it only enhances what the regular season would look like," McCarthy said.

“I’d keep six QBs in the building if it worked.”

Mike McCarthy dismissed the notion that keeping four QBs would take away opportunities to develop the young passers. pic.twitter.com/alWS7XNWhj

The Steelers have invested in developing the position, with Allar selected in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and Howard entering his second season after being selected in the sixth round last year. Rudolph, meanwhile, provides significant NFL experience behind Rodgers.

The potential value of carrying four quarterbacks extends beyond simply having an additional player available on game day. McCarthy believes the competition and preparation within the room can benefit the entire offense throughout the season.

That philosophy also applies to Pittsburgh's quarterback development program.

McCarthy said his quarterback school could "kick up some" once the regular season arrives because the quarterbacks will no longer be working under the same time constraints that exist during training camp practices.

The additional time could allow the Steelers to devote more attention to the finer details of the position, including preparation, communication, film study and offensive concepts.

For a team with a veteran starter in Rodgers and two young quarterbacks in Allar and Howard, that extra developmental work could prove valuable.

The Steelers also have Rudolph, who has experience in Pittsburgh's system and has started games during his NFL career. Keeping all four would give McCarthy a veteran presence behind Rodgers while allowing the organization to continue developing its two younger quarterbacks.

Ultimately, the decision will come down to roster mathematics and how the Steelers believe they can best allocate their available spots.
