title: Baleba completes £70m Man Utd move from Brighton
description: Manchester United sign Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a £70m deal.
fullText:
Manchester United have signed Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a £70m deal.

The Old Trafford club have paid an initial £65m, plus a potential £5m in add-ons, for the 22-year-old, while Brighton have negotiated a sell-on clause.

United targeted Baleba after deciding to strengthen their midfield further following the summer arrivals of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa.

Baleba has signed a five year-contract at Old Trafford, with the option to extend for a further year.

"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams," he said. "Playing at Old Trafford is always special, but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

Baleba's move follows United's shock 2-0 defeat by Hull City in Saturday's Premier League opener, where Santos and Tielemans made their midfield debuts.

United reignited their interest after attempting to sign him last year near deadline day, but were put off by Brighton's valuation, which was in excess of £100m.

Baleba, who joined Brighton from Lille in 2023, is currently sidelined with an ankle injury he picked up during the Seagulls' pre-season training camp in Austria.

He made 112 appearances for Brighton, scoring four times, and 31 in the Premier League last season as they finished eighth to qualify for this season's Conference League.

"Last season was hard," admitted Baleba in a farewell video.

"There was a night against Aston Villa when I came off after 22 minutes. I sat in the dugout and could not lift my head up. You did not boo me. I have thought about that more than you know. You had every reason to and you did not.

"I will be looking for your result every week for the rest of my life. Thank you, Brighton fans."

The move has taken United's summer spending up to £153m as they prepare for a return to the Champions League for the first time since the 2023-24 campaign.

"[He is] a huge talent that the club has been trying to follow for a long time." Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Someone that can improve our team and has different qualities to what we already have in the club.

"The expectation is very high but also we know he is a player we need to give time to become an even better version of himself. We are here to help him set [in] as quick as possible and to help us win games."

What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window?

United will hope for the 2024-25 version of Baleba rather than last season's because it was his performances in that campaign that attracted them.

We can't know what would have happened if the approach for Mateus Fernandes had been successful, nor if Mason Mount had not suffered the injury in the pre-season game with Paris St-Germain two weeks ago that ruled him out of the Premier League opener.

However, even before Saturday's disappointing loss at Hull it is clear that, despite adding Santos and Tielemans to their midfield ranks, they still lack physicality and power.

In theory, Baleba should solve that issue.

The 22-year-old is strong in possession, covers ground quickly, is good in the air and alert to danger.

Crucially, he also has three years' worth of top-flight experience in England behind him, having moved to Brighton from Lille when he was 19. It gives him the edge on Santos, also 22, and it will be interesting to see whether the pair compete for the same place at the base of Michael Carrick's midfield or if, against the best sides, they might play together.

It will also be fascinating to see if he gets asked to fill in at left-back too.

He has played there before and, unlike Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui - who could also switch sides if Luke Shaw is unavailable - is left-footed.

Paul Pogba is the only midfield player United have signed for more than the £70m they are committing to Baleba which, given his age, is a statement in itself.

Baleba's appeal lies less in creativity and 

His 2025-26 campaign was quieter than the previous one, but his 2024-25 numbers show why United have tracked him for so long. He ranked fourth among Premier League midfielders for possessions won in the middle third (107) and interceptions (46), was fifth for ball recoveries (197) and seventh for duels won (199).

That defensive output was matched by his ability to progress possession himself.

Baleba averaged 6.7 progressive carries per 90 minutes, with only three qualifying Premier League defensive midfielders recording more, while 2.9 of those carries travelled at least 10 metres.

His athleticism underpins that game as he reached a top speed of 34.5km/h in 2024-25, compared with 30.5km/h for Casemiro, and averaged 8.2 defensive actions per 90.

He is not necessarily the midfielder United would rely on to dictate possession. Only 11.8% of his passes were classed as line-breaking that season and 22.7% travelled forward - both below the average for central and defensive midfielders.

But that may make him complementary to United's other options rather than a direct alternative. Tielemans can provide more of the progressive distribution, while Baleba offers defensive security and the ability to drive through midfield.

Alongside Kobbie Mainoo, he could take on more of the ball-winning and ground-covering work, while a partnership with Santos could allow Baleba greater freedom to operate box to box.

That versatility is reflected in his positioning as he spent 88% of his minutes last season as a defensive midfielder and 12% in central midfield, suggesting he can anchor the side or step forward depending on who plays alongside him.

United most commonly defended in a 4-2-2-2 last season under Carrick, accounting for 55.9% of their out-of-possession shapes. Baleba's dynamism could be especially valuable in a system where central midfielders are asked to defend large spaces and stop counter-attacks.

There may, however, be an adaptation period.

Baleba is recovering from an ankle ligament injury suffered in pre-season and will need time to recover his match sharpness.

United have also looked to spend longer spells in possession under Carrick, progressing through midfield with quick combinations. Baleba's game is better suited to more open contests, but his passing profile suggests he may need time to adjust to greater responsibility in build-up.

His left foot and mobility should still make him a natural partner for players such as Tielemans or Bruno Fernandes. There is development ahead of him at 22, not least after last season's dip, but at his best Baleba combines defensive activity with the acceleration and carrying power to transform a turnover into an attack within seconds.

title: Fernandes and Shaw win PFA player of the year awards
description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw win the Professional Footballers' Associations men's and women's player of the year awards.
fullText:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw have won the Professional Footballers' Associations men's and women's player of the year awards.

Both were previously named the Football Writers' Association men's and women's footballers of the year for the 2025-26 season.

Fernandes, who last season broke the record for the most assists in a single Premier League campaign with 21, is the first United player to win the award since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

It is a second win in three seasons for Shaw, who secured her third consecutive Women's Super League (WSL) golden boot with 21 goals as Man City were crowned champions.

City defender Nico O'Reilly succeeds Morgan Rogers as men's young player of the year, with the versatile 21-year-old cementing his place in the starting XI.

He contributed eight goal involvements (five goals) and nine clean sheets in 34 league outings, scoring twice, and was named player of the match as City beat Arsenal in the League Cup final.

Arsenal's Olivia Smith retained her crown as the women's young player of the year, becoming only the second player after England international Lauren Hemp, to win the award on multiple occasions.

The Canada international, 22, scored 10 goals in all competitions after joining the Gunners for £1m last summer from Liverpool.

Although it was another trophy-less campaign for Man United, Fernandes enjoyed individual success, surpassing Kevin de Bruyne and Thierry Henry's record of 20 assists in a Premier League campaign.

Fernandes set up his side's opener on the final day of the season against Brighton – and scored their third – to finish 2025-26 with nine goals and 21 assists in 35 league outings. Man City's Rayan Cherki was the second-most prolific provider, with 12 assists.

His haul helped United finish third and secure Champions League football.

In total, the 31-year-old scored nine goals and contributed 22 assists in 37 matches in all competitions.

Fernandes, who joined the club from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020, beat Arsenal trio Gabriel Magalhaes, David Raya, and Declan Rice and Man City attackers Cherki and Erling Haaland to the award.

He is only the second Portuguese to be named player of the year, following back-to-back wins for former Man United winger Cristiano Ronaldo in 2007 and 2008.

Shaw scored 21 goals in 22 appearances as Man City clinched their second WSL title.

The Jamaica international registered hat-tricks against Aston Villa (four goals) and Tottenham and scored twice against West Ham on the final day of the season to become the first player to score 20 or more goals in three different WSL seasons.

Shaw is the first player to win three WSL golden boots, moving clear of two-time winners Vivienne Miedema and Sam Kerr.

The 29-year-old scored a further five goals, including the opener in the final, as Man City won the FA Cup.

Shaw, the third individual to win multiple PFA women's player of the year awards, joining Lucy Bronze and Fran Kirby, previously completed the PFA and FWA double following the 2023-24 campaign.

Team-mate Yui Hasegawa, Aston Villa's Kirsty Hanson, Chelsea's Lauren James, Man United's Jess Park, and Arsenal's Alessia Russo were also shortlisted.

The Premier League team of the year, as voted for by the players, was dominated by champions Arsenal and runners-up Man City.

Arsenal only conceded 27 goals last season, with that impressive record reflected in the selections of goalkeeper Raya and defenders Gabriel, William Saliba and Jurrien Timber named alongside midfielder Rice.

Man City have four representatives – O'Reilly, Cherki, Haaland and Antoine Semenyo – with Man United's Fernandes and team of the year debutant Igor Thiago (Brentford) completing the XI.

The WSL side features three players apiece from champions Man City, Chelsea, and Arsenal, with Man United's Park and Tottenham defender Toko Koga the only players selected from outside the top three sides.

title: Root 'hacked off' and 'disappointed' at Carse incident
description: England captain Joe Root says he is "hacked off" and "disappointed" at the incident involving fast bowler Brydon Carse at a Derby nightclub.
fullText:
England captain Joe Root says he is "hacked off" and "disappointed" at the incident involving fast bowler Brydon Carse at a Derby nightclub.

Carse, 31, was dropped from the squad for the second Test starting against Pakistan this week.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off, I'm really disappointed," Root said in the opening to a news conference.

"After last week's performance, we're sat here and we're talking about something that is not related to it at all."

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has referred the incident to the Cricket Regulator and Carse was replaced in the squad by Sonny Baker, with the Test starting at Lord's on Thursday.

Carse was not on England duty at the time of the incident as he was released to play for Durham, but he is a centrally contracted player.

Root also said he had spoken to his England team-mate about the incident, and expressed his frustration at the "stupid mistakes" that are continually being made.

"I've spoken to Brydon, and when I first found out my main concern was him as a person," Root added.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn by saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure that when he gets his chance he will say that himself.

"But I don't think it's the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

In October, England white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer outside a nightclub in Wellington, New Zealand, with team-mates Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue also present.

During the Ashes tour of Australia, opener Ben Duckett was filmed apparently drunk on England's holiday in Noosa.

And in June, former Test captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and were present when a member of England's security staff was punched by a Saracens rugby player in a London nightclub.

In this latest incident, Carse was with Durham team-mates Stokes and Matthew Potts, all of whom are under England central contracts. In Stokes' case, the England deal remains in place despite his international retirement in June.

It makes a total of eight contracted players who have been involved in or present for late-night incidents in the past year – more than a quarter of the 30 men on England deals.

Punishment to send a shiver needed - Vaughan

England drop Carse after nightclub incident & Pakistan's struggles

When he was reappointed as Test captain, Root confirmed he would remove the midnight curfew which was previously in place during Stokes and Brendon McCullum's regime after a string of off-field incidents during the Ashes over the winter.

Root stood by that decision, saying he still did not think it was "the right way to go", but admitted it would take some time for the team to be trusted by the fans again.

"In many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back, and it's something that we're going to have to live and breathe consistently," he said.

"I might only be in this dressing room for a couple more years, but there is a group of players there who might be in there for another 10.

"We've had a very strong discussion about what's expected of everyone when they play for England, what the standards are that we have to uphold, not just on the field but off it.

"I've made it very clear how we want to conduct ourselves, and now we've got to live it and show people what I see day in, day out in the dressing room, which is a group of characters who know what it means to play for England and not having incidents define how we are seen as players. That's going to take some work and time."

Root also confirmed he had spoken to his predecessor Stokes, who was also seen in the social media video, but only to check in on Carse's wellbeing.

He was asked what potential consequences Carse might face but said he would have no involvement as it is in the hands of the regulator, and was keen to reiterate that he was focusing on moving forward and "building something to be proud of".

"I don't think the recent past has been a good look," Root, 35, said.

"It's our responsibility to change that. I see the dressing room every day and how we operate around cricket and it's very impressive.

"But at the same time, I can understand why we are viewed in a certain way and in a certain light at the moment.

"That's what lies ahead of us, to change that. I just think, if we don't put ourselves in certain situations, it's not something we will have to worry about."

If there was any question as to why England turned to Joe Root for a second stint as Test captain, if he is the right man for the job, then this address at Lord's removed all of those doubts.

Root showed himself to be the leader England need in this moment. Clearly ticking over what happened at the weekend, Root was able to strike the balance between letting his feelings be known, showing compassion for Brydon Carse and not pre-judging the investigation that is ongoing.

There have been plenty of these kinds of news conferences over the past year: someone wearing an England badge explaining a misdemeanour, promising to do better. This time, when Root spoke, his words were plausible and believable.

Some wondered why Root was the one left to face the media, rather than members of the management team like director of cricket Rob Key or chief executive Richard Gould.

Maybe it is because no-one else was able to speak with Root's gravitas. No-one in a suit, not Ben Stokes, nor Harry Brook. Perhaps this is the most impressive display of leadership anyone connected with English cricket has shown for some time.

It should leave no one – especially not the England players – in any doubt where their captain stands on this issue. For any athlete to tell the world they are "hacked off" with a team-mate is a stark message.

Root addressed his England team on Tuesday morning. If the captain was able to speak like this in public, one can only wonder about the sternness of the message delivered in private. Carse would not have been there, but plenty of others who have erred in the past year would have been in the room.

There will be no return for the midnight curfew, but Root was also quite clear about players avoiding situations that could lead to trouble. "Stupid mistakes", he called them. He hammered home the point that players will not find trouble if they do not put themselves in the places where trouble could find them.

But Root also regularly mentioned the notion of this team now having an opportunity to build something on and off the field. Put simply, their reputation in the eyes of the public cannot get much lower, so the only direction is improvement.

Amid all the controversy, English cricket is fortunate to have Root. Not only is he a bona fide all-time great, but also a superb example of how all sportspeople should go about their business on and off the field.

Last week, before his first Test back in charge, Root asked his players to be "good role models and good human beings". They should look no further than their captain for inspiration.

title: Pogacar's astonishing solo effort punishes Vuelta rivals
description: Tadej Pogacar takes a huge step towards winning the Velta a Espana for the first time as he cruises to a resounding victory in the fourth stage on Tuesday.
fullText:
Tadej Pogacar took a huge step towards winning the Vuelta a Espana for the first time and completing his Grand Tour collection as he powered to a resounding victory in the fourth stage on Tuesday.

The Slovenian sped away from his rivals with 50km remaining in Andorra la Vella and finished the 104.8km mountainous stage in two hours 40 minutes 35 seconds, two minutes and 39 seconds ahead of Jarno Widar - the largest margin of victory of Pogacar's Grand Tour career.

He began the day top of the general classification with a nine-second lead and looks increasingly unlikely to relinquish the red jersey, extending his advantage to three minutes and 21 seconds.

"It's super good because now I can be calm and confident for the next days," said Pogacar, who remains on course to become the first rider since 1994 to lead a Grand Tour from start to finish.

"We just keep going day by day and focus on each day after this, because it will be a little bit less stressful for sure.

"I tried with an attack on the climb and I just hoped that I could survive until the finish line. I saw that I could open the gap and I did it and it was pretty tough but a beautiful day out there."

After Monday saw the third stage abandoned because of severe hailstorms in the French Pyrenees, Pogacar began stage four patiently as he sat in the third peloton about 32 seconds behind the leading group.

Lorenzo Fortunato of UCI WorldTeam XDS Astana led across the summit of the first mountain pass to collect the mountain points before Pogacar made his move.

With 50km remaining the UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider surged uphill and began his descent from the second climb with a lead of 90 seconds.

From then on the 27-year-old raced alone and completed the longest Grand Tour solo victory of his career, surpassing the 43km benchmark he set on the the Col du Tourmalet last month en route to winning stage six of the Tour de France.

At one point he stretched his lead to almost three minutes, before a chasing group including Widar and fellow Slovenian Primoz Roglic were able to win some seconds back.

Roglic replaces Wout van Aert - who finished 24 minutes and 35 seconds off the pace - in second place in the general classification, with Spaniard Enric Mas in third.

On Wednesday the 173.3km hilly stage five will start in Falset near Tarragona - the site of more severe hail on Monday - and finish in Roquetes as the Vuelta heads south down Spain's east coast.

title: Cardiff's Anyadike, 15, sets new EFL Cup record as youngest player
description: Cardiff City's Noah Anyadike, 15, becomes the youngest player in EFL Cup history after starting their second-round defeat against Norwich City.
fullText:
Noah Anyadike became the youngest player in EFL Cup history when he started Cardiff City's 2-1 second-round defeat against Norwich City.

The Bluebirds had just completed their second season at the Cardiff City Stadium when the youngster was born - and that is where he made his debut 15 years later.

Without a senior option at centre-back due to an injury crisis, Wales youth international Anyadike was handed his debut at 15 years and 98 days old.

His inclusion from the start saw him break the record previously held by Harvey Elliot, who featured in 2018 for Fulham against Millwall aged 15 years and 174 days.

But in a cruel twist of fate, Anyadike, who also became the youngest player in Cardiff history, hobbled off with a muscle cramp in the second half.

"It was an incredible evening for him and really well deserved. We've been lucky because he's still in school, so he spent so much time with us in the school holidays," said Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy.

Norwich beat Cardiff with Crnac winner on return

"He's making exceptional strides, and he's a very talented player. We were very clear that he was the best option for this game based on how well he's done."

Anyadike is the third player in under 12 months to become Cardiff's youngest player, following Rob Tankiewicz (16 years and 117 days) and Axel Donczew (15 years and 234 days).

But the young defender from Carmarthenshire is not the youngest player in English Football League history.

That honour is still held by Reuben Noble-Lazarus - Barry-Murphy's former Rochdale team-mate - who debuted aged 15 years and 45 days in 2008.

Barry-Murphy, who spent time as Manchester City's youth team boss, understands the role Cardiff have in developing Anyadike as a person and a footballer.

"I think [we] just [have] to expose him to the level of challenge that he's capable of playing and pushing really," he added.

"As you saw, he's very big for his age. He can play at a very high level, so we just have to keep pushing him to make sure that he keeps getting the exposures and the level of challenge he needs.

"And keep educating him on the parts of his game that he needs to improve because he's so young.

"There are always ups and downs for all players at that age when they make their debut.

"Our job now is to make sure that we protect him, educate him, but also push him to make sure that he can have the education and experience that he needs to become a very important player for Cardiff."

Anyadike could make his Championship debut on Saturday when Cardiff host Sheffield United, and may be joined by Gabriel Osho - 13 years his senior - who is expected to return to training on Thursday.

title: PGA Tour play-off shake-up a 'big swing' - McIlroy
description: Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by changing their end-of-season play-offs to matchplay.
fullText:
Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by introducing matchplay to their end-of-season play-offs.

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp confirmed on Thursday that from 2028 the Tour Championship will be played across two weeks, at two different courses, and adopt a head-to-head format.

World number two McIlroy, who is a three-time winner of the FedEx Cup, feels the return of matchplay to the PGA Tour for the first time since 2023 shows fans have been listened to by the decision-makers.

"I think the PGA Tour and the Future Competition Committee and Brian and everyone involved have really taken on board what the fans have been calling for and have wanted, which is matchplay," said the Northern Irishman, 37.

"Brian took me through the plan last week for the first time. I didn't really know anything about it. It's certainly different.

"Two weeks, two different venues, but it's cool. I think they've taken a big swing, and conceptually, I think I really like it."

The FedEx Cup play-offs have have gone through numerous iterations across their two decades, presently consisting of a three-event strokeplay series which begins with the top 70 players from the season-long points list.

This week's concluding Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta will have a $40m (£29.3m) purse, and while the events have undoubtedly been lucrative for players, there have been consistent questions regarding fan engagement.

McIlroy added: "I think they've been great for players. Obviously we play for a ton of money, and it's sort of like the culmination of the entire season.

"The players have been rewarded. I think what the Tour are really trying to do is listen to the fans and what they want, and I think this idea of matchplay over two weeks is something that came mostly from what the people that watch golf wanted, so I think that's a really good thing."

LIV returnees should 'eat humble pie' - Faldo

'Tough road back' to PGA Tour from LIV - McIlroy

The revised play-offs are only part of the changes coming to the PGA Tour in 2028 with a Championship and Challenger series to be established with promotion and relegation between the two.

With a regular season consisting of 15 events and a schedule which will run from February to August, McIlroy hoped more star players primarily based on the PGA Tour will follow his lead and play an increasing number of events on the DP World Tour.

The six-time major winner said: "I think if the PGA Tour are going to play from February through to August, DP World Tour have five months where, with the help of the PGA Tour and maybe some others, [it] can really shine a spotlight on international golf and put on some of the biggest international events in golf.

"I think with what the PGA Tour has been through with changing its competitive model and its structure, I think if the DP World Tour could do something similar, where you host all of your best events in that five-month time frame, it would allow guys to take up membership, to then have something to play for at the end of the DP World Tour season - if they choose to do that."

title: Man Utd's midfield spending is done - now for a left-back?
description: After spending £155m on three midfielders, now Manchester United must decide whether to try to buy a left-back
fullText:
The signing of Carlos Baleba completes a £155m summer revamp of Manchester United's midfield.

At the end of last season, midfield was targeted as a priority area as United looked to build on qualification for the Champions League after a two-year absence.

Baleba arrives along with Andrey Santos, a £48m signing from Chelsea, and £35m former Aston Villa man Youri Tielemans.

It means that, along with England's Kobbie Mainoo, United now have a spread of different attributes across their four-man midfield, three of whom are 22 or younger.

But, at Manchester United, one bad result brings intense pressure.

Even Michael Carrick's calm exterior cracked in a post-match exchange with former Middlesbrough and Swindon Town forward Jan Aage Fjortoft, now a TV presenter for Viaplay, following the shock defeat at Hull when the Norwegian suggested there was a lack of passion in United's ranks.

"Come on, that's ridiculous," replied Carrick. "You played football. You understand. That's a ridiculous thing to say."

So, now the midfield is sorted, it is natural for fans to look at the other areas of Carrick's squad that could do with reinforcements; namely left-back.

Baleba completes £70m Man Utd move from Brighton

Signing an additional left-back has looked an obvious thing for Manchester United to do.

Luke Shaw started all 38 Premier League games last season. He started at Hull. Of United's past 44 league games, the 31-year-old England international has failed to start just one, the final game of the 2024-25 campaign, four days after the Europa League final defeat by Tottenham – and he went on the post-season tour of Asia immediately afterwards.

But, before that, Shaw's injury record had not been great.

Between February 2024 and April 2025, he played as many games for England (three) as he did for his club. He missed three months at the start of the 2023-24 campaign.

There were calf and hamstring issues but also a feeling Erik ten Hag rushed him back too quickly.

More than anyone, Shaw benefited from a 40-game season, allowing him to prepare properly, largely for one game a week, sometimes not even that.

That preparation time will not be repeated.

Although there are blank midweeks between Manchester United's first three games, if they get through two EFL Cup rounds, they will not have a full midweek without a game, other than during international breaks, until the one that includes Christmas Day.

It is the combination of Shaw's injury record and the crush of games that has led to the feeling another left-back will arrive.

There is no doubt the club like Newcastle's Lewis Hall. At 21, he is the right age profile and ideally suited to challenging Shaw for his place, with the safety net of there being enough games to keep both men happy.

However, Newcastle don't want to sell. It would take a huge offer to persuade them otherwise and Manchester United's powerbrokers have proved on numerous occasions this summer they will not be held to ransom, or overpay, for players.

In addition, how much money do they have to spend?

In published third-quarter financial accounts to 31 March, United confirmed they owed £405.75m in outstanding transfer fees, £171.14m of which was due after more than one year. The club are still to outline what the additional $125m (£91.64m) they borrowed in a wider refinancing announced in June will be used for.

The assumption is £70m for Baleba, equal the sum United paid for Casemiro in 2022 and a figure only exceeded in their history in terms of midfielders by the club record £89m spent on Paul Pogba, is at the top end of what they wanted to pay.

Plenty of alternative left-backs to Hall have been mentioned.

Racing Santander's 19-year-old Jorge Salinas has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, but is also coveted by Atletico Madrid.

Barcelona's Alejandro Balde was left out of the 5-0 La Liga victory over Elche by coach Hansi Flick, to allow him to "clear his mind" amid intense transfer speculation, with United among those to be linked with the 22-year-old Spain international. Barcelona are said to value him between €30m (£25.66m) and €40m (£34.22m).

With a week to go before the transfer window closes, the situation is thought to be fluid, but caution in United circles around the expectations of a new left-back being signed is being stressed.

A significant sale could change the dynamic.

However, the idea of Marcus Rashford leaving has virtually been ruled out with confirmation he will wear the coveted number nine shirt this season, while the anticipated exit of Manuel Ugarte had to be scrapped when he was injured at the World Cup.

Of Carrick's senior squad, forward Joshua Zirkzee appears surplus to requirements, yet with fitness doubts over Amad Diallo – the club are choosing to offer no clarification on the extent of his injury amid a report he could be out for up to six weeks – it is uncertain whether interest from Serie A will lead to a sale.

Carrick does have options at left-back without bringing anyone else in. Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have both switched flanks in the past, while Baleba, a left-footed player, has played at full-back for Brighton previously.

In addition, Harry Amass was Shaw's back-up during pre-season and the 19-year-old remains at United. But he was not included in Carrick's squad for the Hull trip and the expectation has been he will leave, either permanently or on loan.

Most still think there will be another left-back in Carrick's squad when the transfer window closes on 1 September – but it is by no means certain.

title: Forest agree £50m deal for Chelsea striker Delap
description: Nottingham Forest have agreed a fee worth around £50m to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.
fullText:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record fee worth around £50m to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old is expected to undergo a medical and sign a long-term contract at the City Ground this week.

Delap's move comes a year after he joined Chelsea from Ipswich Town for £30m amid competition from Manchester United and Everton.

However, Chelsea made him available for sale this summer after he scored just one Premier League goal in a previous campaign disrupted by shoulder and hamstring injuries.

Forest have already signed defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting for £34m, alongside free agents, Austrian midfielder Xaver Schlager and goalkeeper Steve Benda.

They sold England midfielder Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for a club-record £116m and striker Taiwo Awoniyi to Coventry City for £9m.

Delap's arrival would provide competition for strikers Chris Wood and Igor Jesus, who failed to find the target in Forest's 1-0 defeat by Leeds in their home Premier League opener on Saturday.

Chelsea have also signed two strikers this summer in Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg and Danny Welbeck from Brighton.

Delap came up through Derby County's youth system before joining Manchester City in 2019.

After helping City win the FA Youth Cup in the 2019-20 campaign, he scored 24 goals in 20 Premier League 2 matches in 2020-21 as they won the title.

In September 2020 the striker scored on his senior City debut in a 2-1 League Cup win against Bournemouth, and three days later made his Premier League debut in a 5-2 defeat by Leicester.

Injuries played a part in limiting further first-team opportunities, and between 2022 and 2024 Delap spent time on loan in the Championship with Stoke, Preston North End and Hull City.

In the summer of 2024 he was sold for £20m by City to Ipswich and scored 12 goals in 37 Premier League games for the newly promoted side.

title: Alcaraz and Williams thrill in brief but bright US Open mixed doubles showing
description: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz were among the star double-acts in New York as the US Open mixed doubles competition got under way on Tuesday.
fullText:
Enjoy it - and do what Serena Williams tells you to.

That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.

The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.

But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.

Seven-time major winner Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April after injuring his wrist, while 23-time Grand Slam champion Williams was competing in New York for the first time since she "evolved away" from tennis in 2022.

The pair were greeted by huge cheers and were roared on throughout their opening 5-3 4-1 win against Great Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe.

The 44-year-old Williams won the US Open mixed doubles title in its original format alongside Max Mirnyi in 1998 - five years before Alcaraz was born.

Almost 30 years later, Williams still had the competitive desire. She and Alcaraz enjoyed the occasion, playing with smiles on their faces and roaring each other on after winning a point.

Interviewed during a change of ends, Alcaraz said: "I'm playing next to the one and only Serena Williams, so what else can I do? Just enjoy and try to do the things she told me to do."

Their partnership improved rapidly in their first match as they won eight of the final nine games to seal victory.

However, they were denied a place in Wednesday's semi-finals by Italy's world number six Flavio Cobolli and Swiss team-mate Belinda Bencic, who won 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying

Wawrinka 'grateful' despite no US Open wildcard

While Williams will not contest the singles at the US Open - she has not competed in that format since injuring her knee at Wimbledon - Tuesday's matches provided the returning Alcaraz with valuable court time.

The Spaniard admitted he felt nervous before stepping out on the court - in part due to partnering six-time US Open women's singles champion Williams.

"I think everyone could see I was really nervous, I double-faulted on the first point," Alcaraz said after their opening win.

"I was out for almost five months and I almost forgot how it feels stepping out on the court once again.

"It [took] just a couple of games [to settle] and she made it very easy for me to enjoy it and try to go for it."

For Williams, a return to the Arthur Ashe Stadium was something she did not believe would come around again.

"It's always amazing to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said.

"It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."

The controversial revamped mixed doubles format, introduced last year, pits established doubles players against some of the sport's biggest singles stars.

The tournament takes place the week before the singles draw gets under way and allows direct entry into the main draw for top-ranked singles players and wildcards.

Established doubles players such as Britons Glasspool and Henry Patten had to come through two qualifying rounds on Monday.

Top-ranked players Patten and Katerina Siniakova advanced to the quarter-finals before losing to husband-and-wife duo Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina.

Discussing their dynamic, with a semi-final against Cobolli and Bencic to come, Frenchman Monfils said: "I'm a big fan of her game and mentality. Sometimes I think she's ice and I'm the fire.

"We needed to the find the balance. We did today."

The other semi-final will see Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev face Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik.

It was not all plain sailing for the leading singles players, with men's 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffering an early exit at the hands of Patten and Siniakova.

Sabalenka and Djokovic lasted just 49 minutes, but this was otherwise a day where the singles stars edged out the doubles specialists.

With none of the four doubles pairs making it to the last four, the USTA has the sort of semi-final line up it envisaged when deciding to reinvent the mixed doubles 12 months ago.

Sabalenka and Djokovic turned out to be a very brief experiment. The other marquee pairing of Williams and Alcaraz lasted longer, with Williams in particular catching the eye in their first round win.

But with Alcaraz looking increasingly rusty in the quarter-final, Cobolli and Bencic won convincingly.

The Spaniard was wearing a compression sleeve on his right arm, and the skin fade of earlier in the year has been replaced by a mop of black hair.

This was useful court time for him, but did not really tell us anything about his chances of remaining in New York for the singles final in just under three weeks time.

title: Watchdog files bar complaint against Jeanine Pirro over bid to indict 6 Democratic lawmakers
description: A legal watchdog says it filed bar complaints on Tuesday accusing U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro and two lieutenants of violating their ethical duties in seeking to charge six Democratic lawmakers with f...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A legal watchdog says it filed bar complaints on Tuesday accusing U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro and two lieutenants of violating their ethical duties in seeking to charge six Democratic lawmakers with federal crimes for appearing in a video that called on troops to resist unlawful orders.

The Legal Accountability Center's bar complaints, filed in New York and Virginia, claim Pirro and her subordinates, Carlton Davis and Steven Vandervelden, abused their prosecutorial powers to seek "meritless" indictments against President Donald Trump's "perceived political enemies."

Tim Lauer, a spokesperson for Pirro's Washington-based office, noted that it's a grand jury's job — not prosecutors' — to decide whether to hand up an indictment.

"Attempting to weaponize the disciplinary process against prosecutors for doing their jobs amounts to nothing more than a frivolous complaint," Lauer said in a statement.

In February, a grand jury in Washington refused to indict Sens. Mark Kelly and Elissa Slotkin and four House Democrats for urging U.S. service members to follow established military protocols and reject orders they believe to be unlawful. All six lawmakers previously served in the military or at intelligence agencies. Trump accused them of sedition "punishable by DEATH" in a social media post.

A grand jury's refusal to return an indictment is extraordinarily rare, but it has become increasingly common in Washington during Trump's second term. Pirro's critics have accused her of pursuing other legally dubious and politically motivated cases at the Republican president's behest, such as the recently abandoned felony charge against a former Olympian who was accused of defacing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

The center has filed complaints against other Trump administration officials, including Ed Martin Jr., Pirro's predecessor as U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia. Martin has been a leading figure in Trump's campaign to use the Justice Department to prosecute his political opponents.

In its complaint against Pirro, the center asks bar officials to investigate whether she and her colleagues violated rules of professional conduct for attorneys — and to "pursue appropriate discipline" against them. Its complaint against Pirro says her office had no legal basis for its "patently improper effort" to secure an indictment against the six lawmakers.

"The only purpose could have been political animus and a desire to intimidate perceived enemies of the federal government and the President, who personally criticized the lawmakers' video as seditious and punishable by death," the complaint says.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has tried to punish Kelly, a former Navy pilot representing Arizona, for participating in the video. Kelly sued in federal court to block the censure from Hegseth. A district court judge ruled in his favor. Hegseth has asked an appeals court to review the decision.

The center filed its complaint against Pirro and Vandervelden with a grievance committee based in White Plains, New York. In New York, the state Supreme Court's appellate division governs ethical complaints against attorneys. The center filed its complaint against Davis with the Virginia State Bar.

"Prosecutors have enormous power, and with that power comes an obligation to exercise independent legal judgment rather than use the criminal justice system to carry out a president's political demands," the center's co-founder, Michael Teter, said in a statement.

Pirro, who served as a county prosecutor and judge in New York, left her Fox News hosting job to become the top federal prosecutor for Washington last year.

title: A powerful lunar eclipse is coming: What your zodiac sign can expect
description: The sturgeon moon will reach its full phase in the U.S. on Aug. 28.
fullText:
The August full moon, commonly known as the sturgeon moon, is almost here, and this year, it will coincide with a partial lunar eclipse.

Celebrity astrologer Kyle Thomas, who is known for his cosmic guidance for celebrities, businesses, and online influencers, spoke to "Good Morning America" about what the August full moon and lunar eclipse could mean for each zodiac sign.

But first, here's what to know about this month's sturgeon moon.

Next week's partial lunar eclipse caps off a busy month of celestial splendor

The sturgeon moon will reach its full phase at 12:18 a.m. ET on Aug. 28, or 9:18 p.m. PT on Aug. 27, according to the U.S. Naval Observatory.

This year's full moon will also coincide with a partial lunar eclipse, beginning late Aug. 27 and continuing into the early morning hours of Aug. 28.

The best views of the eclipse will be in the eastern United States and Canada and across Central and South America. Those in the western U.S. will still be able to see part of the eclipse.

July's full buck moon is coming: What it means for your zodiac sign

The best time to begin watching the eclipse is around 10:33 p.m. ET on Aug. 27, with the greatest coverage occurring around 12:12 a.m. ET on Aug. 28. The eclipse will end just after 3 a.m. ET.

Unlike a solar eclipse, no special glasses are needed to view a lunar eclipse, and binoculars or a telescope can provide an enhanced view.

The Old Farmer's Almanac, which has been naming full moons since the 1930s, explains that the August full moon is called the sturgeon moon because the giant lake sturgeon, a native freshwater fish of the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain, was historically abundant during this time of year.

The fish was an important food source for Native Americans who lived in the region.

The August full moon is also known by other names associated with the season, including the corn moon, harvest moon and rising moon.

The zodiac sign of each full moon is determined by its position in the night sky relative to the astrological signs. Each year, the moon shifts, resulting in different characteristics, according to Thomas.

This year's sturgeon moon and lunar eclipse will occur in Pisces, the 12th and final zodiac sign. Pisces is a water sign and the opposite sign of Virgo.

"This means that both zodiac signs hold ties to our health -- physical or mental -- as well the physical or spiritual world," Thomas said. "This duality grounds us in the practical while also opening us up to the divine, as well."

Thomas said lunar eclipses can also signal significant turning points.

"Lunar eclipses are three times more powerful and emotional than full moons," he added. "They mark culminations, breakthroughs, or breakdowns, triggering a crisis event that causes us to assess our most internal fears, feelings and actions."

Thomas does not recommend manifesting during an eclipse because he considers eclipse energy intense and unpredictable.

Instead, he recommends using the time to slow down, reflect and pay attention to what is happening in your life.

"Eclipse season is an ideal period in time to journal, pray, relax, center yourself, and practice meditation," Thomas said. "Connecting with nature and spiritual energy are ideal during these times."

Thomas said asking yourself questions rather than using mantras can also be an effective way to engage with the eclipse's energy.

Potential meditations, mantras or journal prompts:

How can I surrender to the flow of the universe?

How can I trust the natural rhythm of life and move gracefully?

How can I release my fears, inhibitions, traumas, and addictions?

How can I lift my spirit to its highest vibration?

Take time to restore your emotional and spiritual energy, Aries.

"This lunation could help you to truly tap into your innate psychic abilities and intuition," Thomas said. "Listen to what the universe is telling you. If you're sensing a hunch, you could be on the right path. Write down any dreams or repeated déjà vu you experience."

Romance and enchantment are in the air, Taurus.

"You'll likely be surrounded by many friends, fans or followers!" Thomas explained. "This lunation spotlights your social network and connections, so you could be attending a milestone event or even meeting many new people. A dearly held hope, aspiration or dream could also be within reach. Last, if you're single, get out there and mingle, or try online dating."

Success could be within reach, Gemini!

"This lunation spotlights your professional world and could bring a promotion, award, accolade or new job offer," Thomas added. "Hustle hard at this time; you'll get very far now. If a job ends near this time, you're being redirected."

New opportunities could be on the horizon, Cancer.

"As the lunation arrives, you could be propelled to swim into new territory," Thomas said. "This may energize you to book a flight and venture out or plan a fun vacation in the year to come. Academic endeavors, legal projects and media or publishing plans could also see a shift now."

Financial gains could be coming your way, Leo.

"A big payout, bonus, scholarship, inheritance or benefits package could be swimming your way," Thomas explained. "This could also bring news around your assets or investments. Last, you'll be feeling quite sensual and intimate near this time, so cozy up with your boo for some TLC."

Relationships take center stage, Virgo.

"A big turning point around a significant relationship could be at hand," Thomas added. "You may move in, make a long-term promise, commit, get engaged or even be wed. Singles could find someone with LTR-potential. However, if you're not aligned, you could go your separate ways."

According to Thomas, the lunation is "cranking your productivity up to hyper speed! You may be polishing off a big project for your employer, taking on more responsibilities or even leaving one job to begin another. Assess your work-life balance to make sure you're not burning yourself out."

Expect a boost in romance and passion, Scorpio.

"The lunation will sing like angels from above," Thomas said. "Romance, passion, pleasure, art, beauty and fertility all shine at this time. Singles may find a soulmate connection or even fall in love. Couples can use this lunation to jazz up their connection for more sugar and spice."

Your focus shifts to home and family, Sagittarius.

"The lunation could cause a shift around your home, real estate, family or parents," Thomas said. "For instance, you may choose to move, redecorate or have a renovation. Others could decide to have a dazzling dinner party that everyone enjoys."

"With this lunation energizing your mind, you could be debuting or working on a major intellectual, writing, speaking, advertising, branding or communications-related project," Thomas said. "Launch your thoughts out into the world and watch who responds to you."

Your finances could be shifting, Aquarius.

"This lunation will likely not only bring money in -- but also cause you to invest it in the right places, too," Thomas explained. "A raise, new client, new job offer or side hustle may appear near this time. If an income stream leaves or changes, use this energy to hustle to new territory."

It's your time to shine, Pisces.

"As the lunation falls in your zodiac sign, you'll be large and in charge!" Thomas said. "A very important personal goal or dream may now be in reach -- as well as a shift around a significant relationship. Now is the moment to step into your power, assert yourself, and show everyone why you're so beautiful, magical and unique."

title: Antisemitic streamer finally makes Dem leader snap with rare rebuke: ‘Malicious’
description: House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries calls Hasan Piker's claim that Jewish Americans invite violence against themselves dangerous and antisemitic.
fullText:
House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York is slamming comments from Hasan Piker after the far-left controversial online streamer suggested that Jewish Americans were inviting violence against themselves over their support for Israel.

"The malicious claim that American Jews are inviting violence against themselves is dangerous and antisemitic," Jeffries charged in a social media post. And he added in a CNN interview on Tuesday that Piker's comments were "malicious" and "should not be tolerated by anyone in the public square."

While Jeffries became the highest-ranking congressional Democrat to fire back at Piker, the criticism from the top Democrat in the U.S. House comes after he has largely stayed silent on the far-left insurgency, backed in part by Piker, that's gripped his party this election cycle.

Jeffries spoke out after Piker, on his stream last week, featured an image of state Sen. Jeremy Moss, the Democratic nominee in Michigan's 11th Congressional District. Moss, who is Jewish, has said that people are sharing a fake audio clip of him claiming that his entire reason for running for Congress is to make sure that America continues to support Israel.

El-sayed Tries To Distance Himself From Hasan Piker After Latest Firestorm

"If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker warned.

Piker, who has over three million online followers, has repeatedly stood by his numerous past comments slamming Israel over its ongoing war against Hamas in Gaza.

Jeffries emphasized in his social media post, "There is zero justification for threats against the safety of our Jewish brothers and sisters at a moment of rising hate. We will fight the cancer of antisemitism with the fierce urgency of now."

Abdul El-sayed Faces Off Wtih Fox News' Jesse Watters In Primetime

Piker's comments were also blasted by Democratic Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich., who charged that Piker is "a hack who thrives on hate."

Rep. Susie Lee, D-Nev., took to X to write, "Claims that American Jews are responsible for the violence being committed against their communities are unacceptable and cannot be tolerated. It's dangerous and antisemitic."

"We must stand up to the scourge of antisemitism wherever it rears its ugly head," Lee added.

Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., praised Jeffries' pushback against Piker.

In an interview on Fox News' "America's Newsroom," Gottheimer called Piker's comments something "right out of the Nazi playbook."

Gottheimer, who is Jewish and a strong supporter of Israel, emphasized, "This is a call for violence against Jews,"

He was also critical of Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan.

Democrats 'Who Never Voted Republican' Backing This Gop Senate Nominee

El-Sayed, who is facing off against former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in battleground Michigan in a high-stakes Senate showdown, on Monday tried to put some distance between himself and Piker, who is a top supporter.

"I want to be crystal clear, nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople," El-Sayed said in a statement.

Gottheimer said that El-Sayed insufficiently pushed back against Piker: "El-Sayed's response was pathetic,"

"No Democratic members should allow Piker anywhere near them on the campaign trail," Gottheimer argued.

Piker endorsed El-Sayed for the Democratic nomination and appeared at some of the candidate's campaign events including a primary night party earlier this month in Detroit, Michigan.

Piker's latest comments were blasted by a growing number of Republicans since they grabbed attention this past weekend, including Rogers, who took aim at both Piker and El-Sayed in a social media post.

"More calls for violence coming out of the El-Sayed campaign," Rogers said on Sunday. And he claimed, "Here is his running mate, Hasan Piker, saying that if AMERICAN JEWS support Israel, they will be violently targeted because of it."

Democracy '26: Stay Up To Date With The Fox News Election Hub

Rogers, who is making a major push to court Democrats in Michigan, added, "Absolutely DISGUSTING. If Abdul El-Sayed had any courage at all, he would call this out and disavow Hasan Piker once and for all. We're waiting, Abdul…"

El-Sayed, in his Monday statement, wrote, "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past."

"My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters. Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk," he added.

What The Latest Fox News Power Rankings In The Midterm Races Show

A former Wayne County Health Department director, El-Sayed, if elected in November, would make history as the nation's first Muslim senator. The epidemiologist who unsuccessfully ran for governor as an insurgent candidate in 2018 has made support for Medicare for all a major component of his campaign and has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

El-Sayed used the word "bloodthirsty" to characterize Israel's military moves in Gaza in an MS NOW interview this month and accused Israeli leadership of genocide against Palestinians. He has argued against unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel, as have other progressive politicians. And El-Sayed has repeatedly declined to directly answer whether Israel has the right to exist.

But El-Sayed has also repeatedly stated that he stands "in solidarity with my Jewish sisters and brothers" to "condemn antisemitism."

title: Former TOPGUN pilot analyzes Marine Corps pilot's eerie calm after emergency F-18 ejection
description: Former TOPGUN pilot Matthew Buckley explains the violent forces of ejection and why Marine Corps Maj. Jackson Simon appeared so calm after his F-18 crash.
fullText:
Former TOPGUN pilot Matthew "Whiz" Buckley told Fox News Digital that the recent crash of a Marine Corps F-18 in Washington state — and the pilot's split-second decision to eject — highlights both the violence of the maneuver and how the ensuing shock can leave an aviator feeling eerily calm.

On June 13, 2026, Marine Corps Maj. Jackson Simon emerged from a wooded area with a bloodied face and walked down the road toward a Yakima County sheriff's deputy, whose bodycam captured the pilot appearing remarkably composed.

"I'm a little frazzled," was about as close as Simon came to expressing fear after his F-18 Hornet crashed into the forest and sparked a small wildfire near Rimrock Lake.

Buckley, who flew F-18 Hornets during his 15-year career in the U.S. Navy, said Simon was likely experiencing a combination of shock, an adrenaline letdown and the effects of training that teaches pilots to compartmentalize under pressure.

Eight Believed Dead After B-52 Crashes Shortly After Takeoff From Edwards Air Force Base

"If anything's going wrong, we focus on the task. Everything else goes away," Buckley told Fox News Digital. "That was the most violent thing that ever happened to that Marine in his entire life."

Buckley served as a pilot in the Navy from 1991 to 2006 and said he was fortunate never to have ejected from an aircraft. The experience can have a devastating toll on the human body.

"Some folks don't go back to flying status. I mean, you can lose a couple inches in height. Your spine compresses. Some people get shorter," Buckley said.

A meta-analysis of more than a dozen studies looking at 1,710 military aircrew ejections found a pooled mortality rate of 10.5%, while 29.8% suffered major injuries. The studies were published between 1971 and 2019.

Army Identifies 2 Pilots Killed In Apache Helicopter Crash Near Fort Hood During Training Exercise

"When you pull that handle, you have two choices: die or maybe live. And I said 'maybe live' because it's incredibly violent. I think the average ejection seat is like 10 to 20 G's of force," Buckley added. "Most folks don't even remember the ejection. They remember pulling the handle and then waking up in their parachute."

Buckley said the pilot's body positioning before the ejection is extremely important in preventing potentially life-threatening injuries. For example, if their arm is extended away from their body, the sudden wind blast could cause it to be "ripped out of the socket."

There's also a phenomenon called "seat slap," which occurs if the pilot does not have their legs flush with the seat prior to ejecting.

"If you look at an ejection seat in a fighter jet, it's rock hard. We're not sitting on a cushion," he said. "If your legs aren't flat on the seat, it could break both of your legs and now you bleed out and die."

Us Navy Identifies Sailor Lost In Arabian Sea After Helicopter's Emergency Water Landing

In some instances, pilots who find themselves in trouble have time to slow their aircraft and perform a controlled ejection, which can reduce the forces involved, Buckley said.

Based on video of the crash, Simon's plane was traveling at a high rate of speed before it struck the trees and exploded, likely leaving little opportunity for a controlled ejection.

Simon had been performing low-flying maneuvers while spectators on the ground watched, according to Kiro 7. After that, his plane reportedly clipped some power lines, which led to it going down.

The Marine Corps has not publicly confirmed that Simon's F-18 struck power lines before the crash and has said the cause of the mishap remains under investigation.

United Airlines Jet Flew Too Low And Too Slow Before Striking Light Pole And Truck Near Newark Airport: Ntsb

According to Buckley, this "clearly" wasn't supposed to happen.

"We have minimum altitude restrictions. And there ain't no 500-foot trees, right? So I don't know what they were doing. It doesn't sound like from his initial statement that there was anything wrong with the airplane. So that's usually not a good sign," Buckley said.

Buckley then speculated about what may have been going through Simon's mind before the crash.

"It looked like a beautiful day. People out on a lake. 'Hey, there's some people down there on the lake. Why don't we go show them what their tax money is [for]? You know, America.' I hope it wasn't something like that," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the third Marine Aircraft Wing, the West Coast-based Marine aviation unit to which Simon's aircraft was assigned.

Buckley said Simon will likely go before a review board that will evaluate his actions surrounding the crash. At the conclusion of the process, the board can recommend what should happen to an aviator's flight status.

If he's found to be at fault, Simon could lose his "wings" or he could be allowed to continue flying, just under what Buckley described as "double secret probation."

"I don't know what the board's gonna do, but it'll come out. It should because...this is a $60 to $65 million Hornet. We deserve to know what happened," he added.

Original article

title: A Montana man killed 8 relatives, including 4 kids, at Sunday dinner, family says
description: A man killed eight of his relatives, including four children, as they gathered for Sunday dinner at a home in Billings, Montana, just weeks after his parents forced him to move out, a family member to...
fullText:
BILLINGS, Mont. (AP) — A man killed eight of his relatives, including four children, as they gathered for Sunday dinner at a home in Billings, Montana, just weeks after his parents forced him to move out, a family member told The Associated Press.

Brad Ireland, whose former wife and two children were among the dead, identified the shooter as 44-year-old Alan Smith. Smith's parents, who were also killed, had asked him to move out, but he returned on Sunday and opened fire, Ireland said.

The victims represented four generations of the blended family, ranging from a great-grandmother in her 90s who used a wheelchair to a 7-year-old girl, according to Jennifer Mercer, a neighbor and family friend who set up an online fundraiser to help cover funeral costs and other expenses, and was authorized to release these details.

Police said they responded to the home on Sunday evening and heard gunshots coming from out back, just before the house was completely engulfed in flames. Investigators confirmed Tuesday there were eight victims, including four children, and that the suspect had suffered a self-inflicted gunshot wound and later died.

The investigation has been complicated by concerns about the structural integrity of the house after the fire burned it to its foundation, said Jeff Stovall, a spokesperson for the Billings Police Department.

Firefighters fought the blaze until around 1 a.m., according to Billings Fire Chief Matt Hoppel. The subdivision where the home was located was outside of municipal limits and not required to have fire hydrants.

Efforts to fight the fire were delayed until the site was secure, allowing the blaze to tear through the home.

Among those killed were Ireland's ex-wife, Megan Ghekiere, and their two children, Owen Ireland, 13, and Chloe Ireland, 7. Also killed were Ghekiere's two stepchildren with her current husband: Landon Ghekiere, 15, and Charlotte Ghekiere, 12.

"The one thing we do know is that Charlotte was the hero," Mercer said. "Charlotte called 911 and she tried to save her family. And that's something the family does want out there."

She described the family as "very loving and close," and said the children all got along and that their parents remained amicable even after divorcing.

"I feel like our entire community is devastated, even people that never knew any of them," Mercer said.

The Smith family was originally from the Seattle area. Ireland said that after he and Megan Ghekiere divorced six years ago, she moved to Montana with their children. That's where she met the man who would become her second husband, who was working and was not at the home when the shooting occurred.

Her parents, Dana and Barb Smith, soon followed, buying a house in Billings near their daughter's home. Evelyn Smith, Dana's elderly mother, lived in a nearby retirement community, Ireland said.

Alan Smith moved in with his parents in Montana and stayed with them for years before being asked to move out a couple weeks ago, Ireland said. He unexpectedly returned to the home on Sunday evening, when the Smiths had gathered for a weekly family dinner.

Ireland said Alan Smith killed his grandmother, his parents, his younger sister and the four children before setting the house on fire. He tried to flee before being confronted by law enforcement, he said.

"There were many red flags and many people spoke out," said Ireland, who lives in Arizona. "No one listened."

Alan Smith was a "hermit" who spent most of his days in his room on his computer, Ireland said.

"No one knew what he did in there 24/7," he said.

Alan Smith had attended Eastern Washington University but had been unable to find or hold a job. A search of criminal records in Montana and Washington found no record Alan Smith had ever been arrested or charged with a crime.

Ireland said that to his knowledge Alan Smith had never been violent, though he could be verbally abusive.

The shootings were the 22nd mass killing this year, according to a database maintained by The Associated Press and USA Today in partnership with Northeastern University.

Fifteen of those have stemmed from domestic disputes, which is higher than the average of about 50% of U.S. mass killings, said James Alan Fox, a criminologist at Northeastern University who manages the database.

The Montana shooting is the deadliest in the U.S. since April, when a Louisiana father fatally shot eight children, including seven of his own, and shot and wounded his wife and another woman.

Biesecker reported from Washington, D.C. Associated Press writers Gene Johnson in Seattle and Mikella Schuettler in Phoenix contributed.

title: Muslim Brotherhood-linked networks embedded across Canadian institutions, new report alleges
description: A new report alleges Muslim Brotherhood-aligned networks have embedded themselves in Canada's elections, universities and civil society institutions.
fullText:
A new report is warning that networks aligned with the Muslim Brotherhood have become deeply embedded in Canada, raising concerns that Islamist influence taking root north of the border could pose a broader threat to the U.S. and Western democracies.

A report from the Institute for the Study of Global Antisemitism and Policy (ISGAP) revealed ties between Muslim Brotherhood-aligned groups and Canadian democratic institutions, civil society, electoral politics and higher education, demonstrating similarities with other activist movements in the West, a phenomenon some analysts have described as the "red-green alliance."

"Canada's challenge is not simply the presence of individual extremist voices or isolated institutional weakness. The report maps how interconnected ideological networks acquire legitimacy, institutional access, public funding, political influence and protection from scrutiny," Charles Asher Small, the research institute's executive director, told Fox News Digital.

Turkey's Nato Role Under Scrutiny Amid New Report On Hamas, Muslim Brotherhood Ties

Small warned that Canadian democracy traditionally has been rooted in openness, notions of citizenship, civil liberties and public trust but has since faced a dynamic of malign foreign influence that could promote ideological entryism, antisemitism and efforts to weaken democratic accountability.

The roughly 200-page report, titled, "Assault on Democratic Values and Principles: How Islamist Entryism Weakens Civil Society and Higher Education in Canada," claimed "numerous apparent links" between the Muslim Association of Canada, a nonprofit based in Mississauga, Canada, and the Muslim Brotherhood, an organization established in Egypt in 1928 by ideologue Hasan al-Banna as part of a wider vision to create a global Islamic caliphate governing nations with rigid interpretations of Islamic law, rules and regulations from the majority Sunni sect.

Watchdog Unleashes Database To Expose 'Loopholes' As $5B In Foreign Cash Floods Us Nonprofits

The report alleged that leaders of the Muslim Association of Canada, one of the largest Muslim charitable organizations in Canada, operating mosques, community centers, schools and educational programs, were "directly or indirectly" associated with the Muslim Brotherhood and that those relationships could influence the charitable organization's activities.

"The ISGAP report is nothing more than recycled Islamophobic tropes dressed up as research. It is a biased, unsubstantiated hit piece that relies on discredited allegations that were themselves challenged by the Ontario Superior Court for their apparent bias," the Muslim Association of Canada told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"The CRA audit has been completed. Preliminary questions raised around any links to the Muslim Brotherhood were dismissed from the CRA's final conclusion," the statement added. "MAC is a solely independent Canadian organization. The ISGAP report amplifies narratives designed to fuel Islamophobia and sow division within Canadian society."

Canadian tax authorities clashed with the Muslim Association of Canada in a 2023 audit, saying that there were indications of ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. The association denied these claims, citing systemic bias and "Islamophobia."

House Committee Passes Foreign Funding Transparency Act To Expose Foreign Donations To Nonprofits

The Canada Revenue Agency ultimately did not revoke the Muslim Association of Canada's tax-exempt charitable status.

The report alleged that Canadian groups affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood assisted in influencing Canada's election system, noting how a coordinated "Vote Palestine" campaign secured endorsements from 344 candidates across four political parties in Canada in the 2025 cycle.

Fox News Digital sat down with Small, who said the report's findings served as a warning sign for potential influence in the U.S.

"The radical left wants to weaken Western or American hegemony, as does radical political Islam," Small explained. "Radical political Islam wants to rid the Islamic world of any influence of the United States, of Europe, of Christianity, of Judaism in its region to ethnically cleanse it."

'Left-wing Extremists,' Cartels Move Into Crosshairs In Trump Terror Shift Beyond Isis

"I think we look back to the Iranian Revolution where the radical left and the Islamists joined together to replace the Shah, and "replace the influence of the United States," he said, referencing the 1979 Iranian Revolution. "It's the same playbook. They're using the same strategy in Europe and now into Canada."

Fox News Digital spoke this past May with Dalia Ziada, a Muslim scholar who was forced to flee Egypt after criticizing Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel. She said that the nexus of radical Islamism with the radical left in the red-green alliance threatened the U.S., American politics and Western society.

Rubio Puts Entire World On Notice Against Rise Of 'Poisonous' Far-left Terror 'Masked As Equality'

"For five or seven years now, we have been seeing some kind of a 'sinful marriage' between the radical left and radical Islamism, the groups that hate Western liberal democracies and desire to destroy them," she told Fox News Digital.

A Fox News Digital investigation found roughly 425 organizations spanning communist groups, Muslim advocacy organizations and anti-Israel activist coalitions are part of a coordinated transnational protest network that collectively brings in about $1 billion in annual revenue.

Elite Universities Face Federal Cash Squeeze Over Millions Tied To China-linked Entities

U.S. government officials in the Trump administration repeatedly have been critical of the Muslim Brotherhood.

Back in January, the Treasury Department designated Egyptian and Jordanian branches of the Muslim Brotherhood as Specially Designated Global Terrorists. In July, the Trump administration sanctioned a senior Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood official who the Treasury Department alleged helped finance Hamas's military wing.

"The Trump administration will relentlessly pursue terrorists and those who finance them," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement in July. "Whether operating under the guise of charities, businesses or underground financial networks, those who enable Hamas will be exposed, sanctioned and held accountable."

The ISGAP report called on the Canadian government to make policy changes to reduce the influence that groups aligned with the Muslim Brotherhood have had in the election system and traditional institutions.

The Embassy of Canada to the United States in Washington did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.
